literature.headline_zh: 禽流感病毒本期文献呈现多方向研究进展
literature.lead_zh: 本期禽流感病毒研究集中呈现以下进展。
key_findings_zh: 研究表明,尽管通过直接液体接种进行有效复制,雾化的 H5N1 菌株在感染人类呼吸道上皮的能力方面表现出显着缺陷。相比之下,无论接种途径如何,原型 H5N1 病毒在雪貂中仍然具有高致病性和致命性。 [10.64898/2026.08.18.745466]
Seo 通过抑制 HIF-1α 信号通路,大大减少了 H9N2 感染的 HD11 细胞中炎症细胞因子 IL-1β、IL-6 和 TNF-α 的产生。在体内,Seo 给药显着改善了 H9N2 感染小鼠的肺部炎症,并增强了肺泡上皮修复,II 型肺泡上皮细胞标记物 Abca3 和 Sftpb 表达增加证明了这一点。 [10.1128/spectrum.02680-25]
潜在类别逻辑模型确定了四种不同的偏好概况,揭示了道德和经济推理中的巨大异质性。 [10.1007/s10198-026-01985-6]
在 400 个样本中,cELISA 检测结果显示 399 个样本(99.75%)呈阴性,其中 1 个样本(0.25%)产生可疑结果。所有样本均显示 HI 效价<8,证实不存在 H5N1 抗体。 [10.1016/j.jevs.2026.106131]
在整个挑战过程中,我们准确地预测了时间趋势和局部 暴发 传播,但无法预测更罕见的长距离传播事件。 [10.64898/2026.08.24.746897]
literature.trend_or_risk_zh: 本期研究方向以入选文献实际覆盖的临床、流行病学、宿主生态、诊断或分子监测主题为准。
literature.headline_en: Recent Avian influenza A viruses literature
literature.lead_en: This reporting window highlights the following research developments.
key_findings_en: The study demonstrated that aerosolized H5N1 strains exhibit a significant defect in their ability to infect human respiratory epithelium, despite efficient replication through direct liquid inoculation. [10.64898/2026.08.18.745466]
Seo greatly reduced the production of inflammatory cytokines IL-1β, IL-6, and TNF-α in H9N2-infected HD11 cells through suppressing the HIF-1α signaling pathway. [10.1128/spectrum.02680-25]
A latent class logit model identified four distinct preference profiles, revealing substantial heterogeneity in moral and economic reasoning. [10.1007/s10198-026-01985-6]

Of the 400 samples, 399 (99.75%) were negative by cELISA, with one sample (0.25%) yielding a doubtful result. All samples showed HI titers of <8, confirming the absence of H5N1 antibodies. [10.1016/j.jevs.2026.106131]
Throughout the challenge, we accurately forecast temporal trends and local outbreak spread, but could not predict rarer, long-distance dispersal events. [10.64898/2026.08.24.746897]
literature.trend_or_risk_en: The direction of this week's research is defined by the clinical, epidemiological, ecological, diagnostic and molecular topics actually represented by the eligible publications.
literature.brief_en: This literature brief prioritizes papers published in the active reporting window and ranks them by relevance, evidence availability, study quality, recency, and independent-source convergence. Detailed study-specific evidence is retained in the article cards below.
brief_items_zh: 本期禽流感病毒研究集中呈现以下进展。
研究表明,尽管通过直接液体接种进行有效复制,雾化的 H5N1 菌株在感染人类呼吸道上皮的能力方面表现出显着缺陷。相比之下,无论接种途径如何,原型 H5N1 病毒在雪貂中仍然具有高致病性和致命性。
Seo 通过抑制 HIF-1α 信号通路,大大减少了 H9N2 感染的 HD11 细胞中炎症细胞因子 IL-1β、IL-6 和 TNF-α 的产生。在体内,Seo 给药显着改善了 H9N2 感染小鼠的肺部炎症,并增强了肺泡上皮修复,II 型肺泡上皮细胞标记物 Abca3 和 Sftpb 表达增加证明了这一点。
潜在类别逻辑模型确定了四种不同的偏好概况,揭示了道德和经济推理中的巨大异质性。 [10.1007/s10198-026-01985-6]。
在 400 个样本中,cELISA 检测结果显示 399 个样本(99.75%)呈阴性,其中 1 个样本(0.25%)产生可疑结果。所有样本均显示 HI 效价<8,证实不存在 H5N1 抗体。
brief_items_en: This reporting window highlights the following research developments.

The study demonstrated that aerosolized H5N1 strains exhibit a significant defect in their ability to infect human respiratory epithelium, despite efficient replication through direct liquid inoculation.
Seo greatly reduced the production of inflammatory cytokines IL-1β, IL-6, and TNF-α in H9N2-infected HD11 cells through suppressing the HIF-1α signaling pathway. [10.1128/spectrum.02680-25].
A latent class logit model identified four distinct preference profiles, revealing substantial heterogeneity in moral and economic reasoning. [10.1007/s10198-026-01985-6].

Of the 400 samples, 399 (99.75%) were negative by cELISA, with one sample (0.25%) yielding a doubtful result. All samples showed HI titers of <8, confirming the absence of H5N1 antibodies. [10.1016/j.jevs.2026.106131].

key_findings_zh: 亚太区域流感网络通过第 19 届国家流感中心和流感 监测 双区域会议强调了针对 禽流感,特别是 HPAI A(H5N1) 的准备。世界卫生组织(WHO)报道了这一事件。 [news-aa651ce5bf3ff113]

news.headline_en: Recent Avian influenza A viruses news
news.lead_en: This reporting window highlights the following Avian influenza A viruses news developments.
key_findings_en: The Asia-Pacific regional influenza network emphasized preparedness for avian influenza, particularly HPAI A(H5N1), through the 19th Biregional Meeting of National Influenza Centres and Influenza Surveillance. The event was reported by the World Health Organization (WHO). [news-aa651ce5bf3ff113]

The supplied text is a PAHO webpage listing that references a news item titled 'Avian influenza in the Americas: animal outbreaks decline, but PAHO calls for continued vigilance' dated 27 Aug 2026, and an associated Epidemiological Update 'Avian Influenza A(H5) in the Americas Region' dated 26 Aug 2026. [news-4f876f7b18383c8a]

An epidemiological update on avian influenza A(H5) viruses, including the A(H5N1) subtype and other avian influenza A(H5) viruses, was reported by PAHO. The update details the spread of these viruses in birds and mammals, with a note on the global public health risk being low. [news-af645e96574d0fb3]

Shingles vaccine linked to lower risk of heart disease for 7 years Meghan Holohan Relative to the discontinued live vaccine, the recombinant vaccine may better protect people from more than an uncomfortable infection. [news-1004dc40b8935ebb]

The World Health Organisation (WHO) issued an alert about the rising threat of H5N1 bird flu in the Asia-Pacific region, emphasizing the need for vigilance and preparedness. This is a confirmed event based on WHO's official warning and meeting outcomes. [news-8f702056c931de3c]

papers.title: IMPAIRED NEURAMINIDASE AND POLYMERASE ACTIVITIES CORRESPOND WITH LIMITED AEROSOL INFECTIVITY OF B3.13 AND D1.1 H5N1 LINEAGES IN HUMAN RESPIRATORY CULTURES
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT The ongoing panzootic of clade 2.3.4.4b highly pathogenic avian influenza (HPAI) H5N1 viruses has reached a critical point, marked by unprecedented mammalian spillover and sustained outbreaks in U.S. While these viruses remain highly lethal in traditional ferret models, human infections—primarily linked to the B3.13 and D1.1 lineages—have been notably mild, typically presenting as conjunctivitis with minimal respiratory involvement. In this study, we address this disconnect by evaluating the infectivity of recent H5N1 isolates using a physiologically relevant air-liquid interface (ALI) culture system that incorporates an aerosol settling chamber. We demonstrate that while direct liquid inoculation leads to efficient replication, aerosolized H5N1 strains exhibit a significant defect in their ability to infect human respiratory epithelium. In contrast, a prototypic H5N1 virus remains highly pathogenic and lethal in ferrets regardless of the inoculation route, showing systemic dissemination to the brain and other organs. Our findings identify two primary viral determinants driving this respiratory restriction: reduced neuraminidase (NA) enzymatic activity and impaired polymerase activity. Collectively, these results suggest that commonly used mammalian models may overstate current human pandemic risk. This work highlights the critical need for alternative risk- assessment platforms to identify the specific genetic shifts required for these viruses to overcome existing barriers to human adaptation. IMPORTANCE Current pandemic risk assessments rely heavily on animal models, particularly ferrets, to evaluate the threat posed by emerging influenza viruses. However, recent H5N1 viruses that have caused predominantly mild human infections have remained highly virulent in these models, creating uncertainty about how well they predict human disease. Using a physiologically relevant human airway model infected through aerosol exposure, we demonstrate that contemporary H5N1 are markedly restricted in their ability to establish respiratory infection despite retaining high virulence in ferrets. These findings highlight the importance of incorporating human airway aerosol models into pandemic risk assessment frameworks to better evaluate the human adaptation and respiratory infection potential of emerging influenza viruses.

source_records.abstract: ABSTRACT The ongoing panzootic of clade 2.3.4.4b highly pathogenic avian influenza (HPAI) H5N1 viruses has reached a critical point, marked by unprecedented mammalian spillover and sustained outbreaks in U.S. While these viruses remain highly lethal in traditional ferret models, human infections—primarily linked to the B3.13 and D1.1 lineages—have been notably mild, typically presenting as conjunctivitis with minimal respiratory involvement. In this study, we address this disconnect by evaluating the infectivity of recent H5N1 isolates using a physiologically relevant air-liquid interface (ALI) culture system that incorporates an aerosol settling chamber. We demonstrate that while direct liquid inoculation leads to efficient replication, aerosolized H5N1 strains exhibit a significant defect in their ability to infect human respiratory epithelium. In contrast, a prototypic H5N1 virus remains highly pathogenic and lethal in ferrets regardless of the inoculation route, showing systemic dissemination to the brain and other organs. Our findings identify two primary viral determinants driving this respiratory restriction: reduced neuraminidase (NA) enzymatic activity and impaired polymerase activity. Collectively, these results suggest that commonly used mammalian models may overstate current human pandemic risk. This work highlights the critical need for alternative risk- assessment platforms to identify the specific genetic shifts required for these viruses to overcome existing barriers to human adaptation. IMPORTANCE Current pandemic risk assessments rely heavily on animal models, particularly ferrets, to evaluate the threat posed by emerging influenza viruses. However, recent H5N1 viruses that have caused predominantly mild human infections have remained highly virulent in these models, creating uncertainty about how well they predict human disease. Using a physiologically relevant human airway model infected through aerosol exposure, we demonstrate that contemporary H5N1 are markedly restricted in their ability to establish respiratory infection despite retaining high virulence in ferrets. These findings highlight the importance of incorporating human airway aerosol models into pandemic risk assessment frameworks to better evaluate the human adaptation and respiratory infection potential of emerging influenza viruses.

analysis.study_design_and_population: This study used a physiologically relevant air-liquid interface (ALI) culture system with an aerosol settling chamber to assess the infectivity of recent H5N1 isolates. The study was conducted in a laboratory setting and focused on human respiratory epithelium.
analysis.methods: The researchers evaluated the infectivity of recent H5N1 isolates using a human airway model infected through aerosol exposure. They incorporated an aerosol settling chamber to simulate realistic conditions and assessed viral replication and dissemination.
analysis.main_results: The study demonstrated that aerosolized H5N1 strains exhibit a significant defect in their ability to infect human respiratory epithelium, despite efficient replication through direct liquid inoculation. analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The results suggest that the respiratory restriction observed in contemporary H5N1 viruses is due to reduced neuraminidase (NA) enzymatic activity and impaired polymerase activity, which are key viral determinants. analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its reliance on a single human airway model and does not account for other potential host factors. analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the limited aerosol infectivity of recent H5N1 lineages, specifically B3.13 and D1.1, in human respiratory cultures. It highlights the discrepancy between the high virulence of these viruses in traditional ferret models and the mild human infections they cause. Using a physiologically relevant air-liquid interface (ALI) system with an aerosol settling chamber, the researchers demonstrate that aerosolized H5N1 strains have significant defects in infecting human respiratory epithelium, unlike direct liquid inoculation. The study identifies reduced neuraminidase (NA) activity and impaired polymerase function as key factors contributing to this restriction. These findings suggest that current animal models may overestimate human pandemic risk and underscore the need for alternative platforms that better reflect human infection dynamics. The study's results are robust but limited by the use of a single human airway model, which may not fully capture the complexity of human host responses.

papers.abstract_zh: 摘要 进化枝 2.3.4.4b 高致病性禽流感 (HPAI) H5N1 病毒的持续流行已达到临界点,其特点是史无前例的哺乳动物 跨物种溢出 和美国持续的 暴发。虽然这些病毒在传统雪貂模型中仍然具有高度致命性,但人类感染(主要与 B3.13 和 D1.1 谱系有关)明显较轻,通常表现为结膜炎,很少累及呼吸道。在这项研究中,我们通过使用包含气溶胶沉降室的生理相关气液界面 (ALI) 培养系统评估最近 H5N1 分离株的感染性来解决这种脱节问题。我们证明,虽然直接液体接种可实现有效复制,但雾化 H5N1 菌株在感染人类呼吸道上皮的能力方面表现出显着缺陷。相比之下,无论接种途径如何,原型 H5N1 病毒在雪貂中仍然具有高致病性和致命性,显示出系统性传播到大脑和其他器官。我们的研究结果确定了导致这种呼吸限制的两个主要病毒决定因素:神经氨酸酶(NA)酶活性降低和聚合酶活性受损。总的来说,这些结果表明常用的哺乳动物模型可能夸大了当前人类大流行的风险。这项工作强调了对替代风险评估平台的迫切需要,以确定这些病毒所需的特定基因转变,以克服人类适应的现有障碍。重要性 当前的大流行风险评估在很大程度上依赖动物模型,特别是雪貂,来评估新出现的流感病毒造成的威胁。然而,最近主要引起轻度人类感染的 H5N1 病毒在这些模型中仍然具有高毒力,这给它们预测人类疾病的能力带来了不确定性。使用通过气溶胶暴露感染的生理相关人类气道模型,我们证明,尽管在雪貂中保留了高毒力,但当代 H5N1 建立呼吸道感染的能力明显受到限制。这些发现强调了将人类气道气溶胶模型纳入大流行风险评估框架的重要性,以更好地评估人类适应和新兴流感病毒的呼吸道感染潜力。

papers.title: Hypoxia-inducible factor 1-alpha inhibition mitigates inflammatory responses induced by H9N2 avian influenza virus.
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT H9N2 avian influenza virus (AIV) poses significant threats to poultry and public health, with the potential to contribute to the emergence of more virulent influenza strains. Hypoxia-inducible factor 1-alpha (HIF-1α) plays a crucial role in viral pathogenesis, immune regulation, and inflammation, making it a promising target for therapeutic intervention. Here, we explored the involvement of HIF-1α in H9N2 AIV pathogenesis and associated inflammatory responses. Our data revealed that HIF-1α exacerbates inflammation induced by H9N2 AIV infection through its regulation of mitochondrial fitness. Additionally, we investigated Sotetsuflavone (Seo), a naturally derived flavonoid, for its potential to modulate inflammatory responses following H9N2 infection. Molecular docking coupled with surface plasmon resonance assays indicated that Seo exhibits robust binding affinity to HIF-1α, implying a direct inhibitory mechanism. Subsequent in vitro studies demonstrated that Seo greatly reduced the production of inflammatory cytokines, including IL-1β, IL-6, and TNF-α, through suppressing the HIF-1α signaling pathway in HD11 cells infected with H9N2 AIV. Correspondingly, in vivo experiments established that Seo administration significantly ameliorated pulmonary inflammation in H9N2-infected mice, while also enhancing alveolar epithelial repair, as evidenced by increased expression of type II alveolar epithelial cell markers Abca3 and Sftpb. Collectively, these findings identify Seo as a potent inhibitor of HIF-1α, highlighting its therapeutic potential in mitigating inflammation and lung damage associated with influenza virus infection. IMPORTANCE H9N2 avian influenza virus triggers inflammatory lung injury via hypoxia-inducible factor-1 alpha (HIF-1α)-mediated dysregulation of mitochondrial function. The natural flavonoid Sotetsuflavone (Seo) directly binds and inhibits HIF-1α, as confirmed by molecular docking and surface plasmon resonance assays. In H9N2-infected HD11 cells, Seo suppresses HIF-1α signaling, reducing IL-1β, IL-6, and TNF-α production. In vivo , Seo treatment attenuates pulmonary inflammation and enhances alveolar epithelial repair in mice, upregulating type II pneumocyte markers (Abca3 and Sftpb). These findings identify Seo as a promising HIF-1α-targeted therapeutic for influenza-associated immunopathology.

papers.title_zh: 缺氧诱导因子 1-α 抑制可减轻 H9N2 禽流感 病毒诱导的炎症反应。
papers.source_body_en: ABSTRACT H9N2 avian influenza virus (AIV) poses significant threats to poultry and public health, with the potential to contribute to the emergence of more virulent influenza strains. Hypoxia-inducible factor 1-alpha (HIF-1α) plays a crucial role in viral pathogenesis, immune regulation, and inflammation, making it a promising target for therapeutic intervention. Here, we explored the involvement of HIF-1α in H9N2 AIV pathogenesis and associated inflammatory responses. Our data revealed that HIF-1α exacerbates inflammation induced by H9N2 AIV infection through its regulation of mitochondrial fitness. Additionally, we investigated Sotetsuflavone (Seo), a naturally derived flavonoid, for its potential to modulate inflammatory responses following H9N2 infection. Molecular docking coupled with surface plasmon resonance assays indicated that Seo exhibits robust binding affinity to HIF-1α, implying a direct inhibitory mechanism. Subsequent in vitro studies demonstrated that Seo greatly reduced the production of inflammatory cytokines, including IL-1β, IL-6, and TNF-α, through suppressing the HIF-1α signaling pathway in HD11 cells infected with H9N2 AIV. Correspondingly, in vivo experiments established that Seo administration significantly ameliorated pulmonary inflammation in H9N2-infected mice, while also enhancing alveolar epithelial repair, as evidenced by increased expression of type II alveolar epithelial cell markers Abca3 and Sftpb. Collectively, these findings identify Seo as a potent inhibitor of HIF-1α, highlighting its therapeutic potential in mitigating inflammation and lung damage associated with influenza virus infection. IMPORTANCE H9N2 avian influenza virus triggers inflammatory lung injury via hypoxia-inducible factor-1 alpha (HIF-1α)-mediated dysregulation of mitochondrial function. The natural flavonoid Sotetsuflavone (Seo) directly binds and inhibits HIF-1α, as confirmed by molecular docking and surface plasmon resonance assays. In H9N2-infected HD11 cells, Seo suppresses HIF-1α signaling, reducing IL-1β, IL-6, and TNF-α production. In vivo , Seo treatment attenuates pulmonary inflammation and enhances alveolar epithelial repair in mice, upregulating type II pneumocyte markers (Abca3 and Sftpb). These findings identify Seo as a promising HIF-1α-targeted therapeutic for influenza-associated immunopathology.

papers.title: Forecasting high pathogenicity avian influenza with a stochastic mechanistic model: performance and lessons for Australia
papers.abstract: High pathogenicity avian influenza (HPAI) H5N1 clade 2.3.4.4b has caused a global panzootic with unprecedented impacts on wildlife and livestock, making evidence-based disease mitigation and outbreak response critical. In this paper, we describe a spatiotemporal mechanistic model of infectious disease dynamics developed for the HPAI Modelling Challenge and its implications for forecasting and policy in Australia. To emulate emergency response conditions, we adapted an existing model for rapid deployment rather than developing a bespoke model. We refined the model iteratively across the challenge to better analyse the provided outbreak data. Throughout the challenge, we accurately forecast temporal trends and local outbreak spread, but could not predict rarer, long-distance dispersal events. The challenge ended before HPAI H5N1 was first detected in Australia (June 2026), providing a critical opportunity to test our response modelling readiness for an incursion in wildlife and potential spillover into commercial poultry. Our experience identifies three key considerations for Australia's HPAI H5N1 preparedness: targeted enhancements to our model to improve forecast precision and enable scenario-based policy evaluation; the critical value of pre-existing modelling infrastructure for rapid emergency response; and sustained collaboration between research and policy institutions to align modelling capabilities with outbreak response requirements.

papers.title: Mammary Gland Tropism and Milk-Mediated Transmission of H5N1 in Dairy Cattle: Implications for One Health Surveillance
papers.abstract: Highly pathogenic avian influenza H5N1 virus (H5N1 HPAIV) has long circulated in wild waterfowl and poultry and continues to cross species barriers, posing sustained threats to livestock productivity and public health. The 2024 outbreak of H5N1 HPAIV in dairy cattle across multiple U.S. states represents the first recognized large-scale transmission event of this virus in ruminants, reshaping our understanding of its host range and transmission ecology. This review summarizes recent advances in the epidemiology, virological characteristics, transmission, pathogenesis, surveillance, and control of dairy cattle-associated H5N1. The initial multistate outbreak was dominated by clade 2.3.4.4b genotype B3.13, whereas subsequent independent introductions of genotype D1.1 demonstrated that repeated avian-to-cattle spillover also contributes to the evolving outbreak ecology. A defining feature is efficient replication in bovine mammary epithelial cells, resulting in high viral titers in milk, supporting milk-associated exposure and milking-related contamination as plausible components of transmission, although the relative contribution of different routes remains unresolved. Infected cattle typically show reduced feed intake, a marked decline in milk production, abnormal milk, and mild systemic signs, whereas severe respiratory disease and mortality are uncommon. Mutations such as PB2-M631L, PA-K497R, and changes in NP and NS1 may promote replication and immune evasion in bovine cells, while genotype-specific PB2 adaptations highlight the potential for further mammalian adaptation. Human infections reported to date have been predominantly mild and associated with occupational exposure, with no evidence of sustained human-to-human transmission. Experimental vaccine studies have begun to demonstrate immunogenicity in cattle, although protection against mammary infection, viral shedding, and transmission remains to be established. Future priorities include clarifying mammary tropism and transmission dynamics, while strengthening diagnostics, farm biosecurity, vaccination, evaluating cattle vaccination strategies, and integrated One Health surveillance.

papers.abstract_zh: 高致病性禽流感 H5N1 病毒(H5N1 HPAIV)长期在野生水禽和家禽中传播,并继续跨越物种障碍,对牲畜生产力和公共卫生构成持续威胁。2024 年美国多个州奶牛中 H5N1 HPAIV 的 暴发 代表了该病毒在反刍动物中首次被认可的大规模 传播 事件,重塑了我们对其 宿主 系列和 传播 生态的理解。本综述总结了 流行病学、病毒学特征、传播、发病机制、监测 以及奶牛相关 H5N1 控制方面的最新进展。最初的多态 暴发 由进化枝 2.3.4.4b 基因型 B3.13 主导,而随后独立引入的基因型 D1.1 表明,重复的禽类到牛 跨物种溢出 也有助于不断发展的 暴发 生态。一个决定性特征是在牛乳腺上皮细胞中有效复制,导致牛奶中病毒滴度较高,支持与牛奶相关的暴露和挤奶相关的污染作为 传播 的合理成分,尽管不同途径的相对贡献仍未解决。受感染的牛通常表现出采食量减少、产奶量显着下降、产奶量异常和轻微的全身症状,而严重的呼吸道疾病和 死亡率 并不常见。突变(例如PB2-M631L、PA-K497R)以及NP和NS1的变化可能会促进牛细胞的复制和免疫逃避,而基因型特异性的PB2适应则凸显了哺乳动物进一步适应的潜力。迄今为止报告的人类感染主要是轻微的,并且与职业暴露有关,没有证据表明存在持续的人传人 传播。实验性 疫苗 研究已开始证明牛的免疫原性,但针对乳腺感染、病毒脱落和 传播 的保护作用仍有待确定。未来的优先事项包括澄清向乳性和 传播 动态,同时加强诊断、农场生物安全、疫苗接种、评估牛 疫苗接种 策略以及综合 One Health 监测。

papers.title: No evidence of H5N1 avian influenza virus infection in Japanese horses in 2025.
papers.abstract: The global spillover of clade 2.3.4.4b H5N1 highly pathogenic avian influenza virus into mammalian hosts has become a public health concern as well as to the equine industry. However, previous reports on H5N1 natural infection and the presence of specific antibodies in horses remain limited. Therefore, we conducted a serosurveillance study to assess the prevalence of H5N1 antibodies collected from 400 horses in Japan. Samples were screened using competitive ELISA (cELISA) and hemagglutination inhibition (HI) tests against H5-recombinant protein and H5N1 viral antigen, respectively. Of the 400 samples, 399 (99.75%) were negative by cELISA, while one sample (0.25%) yielded a doubtful result. However, all samples showed HI titers of <8, confirming the absence of H5N1 antibodies. These findings indicate that the current risk of H5N1 infection among horses in Japan remains limited. Nonetheless, continuous global surveillance is warranted to monitor the potential risk of H5N1 spillover into equine populations.

papers.title_zh: 2025 年,没有证据表明日本马感染 H5N1 禽流感 病毒。
papers.source_body_en: The global spillover of clade 2.3.4.4b H5N1 highly pathogenic avian influenza virus into mammalian hosts has become a public health concern as well as to the equine industry. However, previous reports on H5N1 natural infection and the presence of specific antibodies in horses remain limited. Therefore, we conducted a serosurveillance study to assess the prevalence of H5N1 antibodies collected from 400 horses in Japan. Samples were screened using competitive ELISA (cELISA) and hemagglutination inhibition (HI) tests against H5-recombinant protein and H5N1 viral antigen, respectively. Of the 400 samples, 399 (99.75%) were negative by cELISA, while one sample (0.25%) yielded a doubtful result. However, all samples showed HI titers of <8, confirming the absence of H5N1 antibodies. These findings indicate that the current risk of H5N1 infection among horses in Japan remains limited. Nonetheless, continuous global surveillance is warranted to monitor the potential risk of H5N1 spillover into equine populations.

papers.title: Understanding moral trade-offs in pandemic response: A discrete choice experiment on avian influenza policies.
papers.abstract: Abstract Pandemic preparedness requires navigating trade-offs between health, economic, and social impacts; choices that often involve moral tensions. This study investigates how the Dutch public evaluates such trade-offs in the context of a potential outbreak of highly pathogenic avian influenza (HPAI). Using a discrete choice experiment (DCE) administered to a representative sample of 1,045 respondents from the LISS panel, we examined preferences across six policy outcomes: mortality, lasting physical and mental injuries, postponed healthcare, social restrictions, and one-off tax payments. A latent class logit model identified four distinct preference profiles, revealing substantial heterogeneity in moral and economic reasoning. Two classes exhibited taboo trade-off aversion (TTOA) when values such as life or human dignity were traded against monetary costs. Respondents displaying TTOA emphasized solidarity and governmental responsibility, while cost-sensitive groups prioritized economic efficiency. These findings highlight that public acceptance of pandemic policies depends not only on effectiveness and cost but also on perceived moral legitimacy. Accounting for TTOA in economic evaluation can improve the ethical considerations and societal acceptability of future pandemic preparedness strategies.

analysis.summary_en: This study explores how the Dutch public evaluates moral trade-offs in pandemic response policies related to avian influenza. Using a discrete choice experiment with 1,045 respondents, the research identifies varying preferences across six policy outcomes, including mortality, injuries, healthcare delays, social restrictions, and tax payments. The results reveal four distinct preference profiles, highlighting substantial differences in moral and economic reasoning. Two groups showed aversion to trading life or human dignity for monetary costs, while others prioritized economic efficiency. The study emphasizes that public acceptance of pandemic policies depends on perceived moral legitimacy, not just effectiveness and cost. These findings suggest that incorporating moral considerations, such as taboo trade-off aversion, into economic evaluations can enhance the ethical and societal acceptability of future pandemic preparedness strategies. The study's design, based on a representative sample and latent class modeling, provides insights into public preferences but may have limitations in capturing the full complexity of moral reasoning.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 流行病防范需要在健康、经济和社会影响之间进行权衡;往往涉及道德紧张的选择。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 本研究调查了荷兰公众如何在 高致病性禽流感 (HPAI) 的潜在 暴发 背景下评估此类权衡。
elements_zh.methods: 通过对 LISS 小组中 1,045 名受访者的代表性样本进行离散选择实验 (DCE),我们检查了六种政策结果的偏好:死亡率、持久的身体和精神伤害、推迟医疗保健、社会限制和一次性纳税。
elements_zh.main_results: 潜在类别逻辑模型确定了四种不同的偏好概况,揭示了道德和经济推理中的巨大异质性。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 当生命或人类尊严等价值与金钱成本进行交易时,两个阶层表现出禁忌权衡厌恶(TTOA)。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 显示 TTOA 的受访者强调团结和政府责任,而对成本敏感的群体则优先考虑经济效率。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 这些发现强调,公众对流行病政策的接受程度不仅取决于有效性和成本,还取决于感知的道德合法性。

papers.title: Exploring integrated advice and avian influenza knowledge gaps by using a Highly Pathogenic Avian Influenza outbreak simulation.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Initial evaluations of the COVID-19 pandemic suggested that broad multidisciplinary expertise is needed for an all of society pandemic response. However, it is unclear whether balanced, multi-perspective scientific advising is secured in separate disciplinary advisory committees. AIM: Our aim was to explore the potential of integrated advising among biomedical, societal and economic experts into pandemic response, using a simulation of a highly pathogenic avian influenza (HPAI) outbreak. Additionally, we aimed to identify cross-cutting gaps in knowledge and expertise relevant for HPAI pandemic preparedness. METHODS: We conducted two table-top simulation exercises (April/May 2024), based on a fictitious HPAI outbreak originating in the Netherlands and associated with severe disease among children. In total, 22 and 19 experts participated, representing biomedical, societal and economic sciences. Participants first drafted an outbreak management advice in separate biomedical and societal teams, followed by integrated deliberations and advice in mixed groups. Written notes of the deliberations and pre-simulation interviews was used for an inductive, reflexive thematic analysis. RESULTS: Separate advisory processes differed in perceived urgency, situation assessment, and the drafted best- and worst-case scenarios. Mixed groups deliberations exposed disciplinary blind spots and fostered mutual understanding. In particular, school closure was discussed extensively due to conflicting perspectives. Cross-cutting knowledge and know-how gaps were identified in the alignment of (infra)structures and guidelines. CONCLUSIONS: Our simulation exercises suggest that an integrated advisory approach may have an added value in overcoming conflicting advice during pandemics. Further research is needed to explore whether this observed added value extends to an integrated advisory body.

analysis.summary_en: This study used a simulation of a highly pathogenic avian influenza (HPAI) outbreak to explore the potential of integrated advising among biomedical, societal, and economic experts in pandemic response. Two table-top exercises were conducted in April/May 2024, involving 22 and 19 experts, respectively. The analysis revealed differences in advice from separate disciplinary teams and highlighted the value of mixed-group deliberations in fostering mutual understanding and identifying cross-cutting knowledge gaps. The study emphasizes the need for further research to determine if integrated advisory bodies can enhance pandemic preparedness. Key findings include the importance of aligning (infra)structures and guidelines across disciplines and the need to address conflicting perspectives, such as those surrounding school closures during outbreaks.

elements_zh.scope_and_question: 该研究旨在利用 高致病性禽流感 (HPAI) 暴发 的模拟,探索生物医学、社会和经济专家在流行病应对方面提供综合建议的潜力。它还试图确定与高致病性禽流感大流行防范相关的跨领域知识和专业知识差距。
elements_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 该审查涉及 2024 年 4 月/5 月进行的两次桌面模拟练习,基于源自荷兰且与儿童严重疾病相关的虚构 HPAI 暴发。共有 22 名和 19 名来自生物医学、社会和经济科学领域的专家参加。使用归纳、反思性主题分析对审议和预模拟访谈的书面记录进行了分析。
elements_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 模拟练习表明,综合咨询方法可能会在克服大流行期间相互冲突的建议方面提供附加值。混合小组审议暴露了纪律盲点并促进了相互理解,特别是在因观点冲突而关闭学校的问题上。在(基础)结构和指南的协调中确定了跨领域的知识和技术差距。
elements_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 单独的咨询流程在紧迫性、情况评估以及起草的最佳和最坏情况方面有所不同。该研究强调需要进一步研究,以确定观察到的综合咨询的附加价值是否延伸到实际的综合咨询机构。
elements_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 需要进一步研究来探索观察到的综合咨询的附加价值是否延伸到综合咨询机构。研究结果表明,跨学科调整(基础设施)结构和指南对于解决大流行病防范方面的知识差距非常重要。

AIM: Our aim was to explore the potential of integrated advising among biomedical, societal and economic experts into pandemic response, using a simulation of a highly pathogenic avian influenza (HPAI) outbreak. Additionally, we aimed to identify cross-cutting gaps in knowledge and expertise relevant for HPAI pandemic preparedness. METHODS: We conducted two table-top simulation exercises (April/May 2024), based on a fictitious HPAI outbreak originating in the Netherlands and associated with severe disease among children. In total, 22 and 19 experts participated, representing biomedical, societal and economic sciences. Participants first drafted an outbreak management advice in separate biomedical and societal teams, followed by integrated deliberations and advice in mixed groups. Written notes of the deliberations and pre-simulation interviews was used for an inductive, reflexive thematic analysis. RESULTS: Separate advisory processes differed in perceived urgency, situation assessment, and the drafted best- and worst-case scenarios. Mixed groups deliberations exposed disciplinary blind spots and fostered mutual understanding. In particular, school closure was discussed extensively due to conflicting perspectives. Cross-cutting knowledge and know-how gaps were identified in the alignment of (infra)structures and guidelines. CONCLUSIONS: Our simulation exercises suggest that an integrated advisory approach may have an added value in overcoming conflicting advice during pandemics. Further research is needed to explore whether this observed added value extends to an integrated advisory body.
papers.abstract_zh: 背景:对 COVID-19 大流行的初步评估表明,全社会应对大流行需要广泛的多学科专业知识。然而,目前尚不清楚独立的学科咨询委员会是否能够提供平衡、多视角的科学建议。目的:我们的目标是利用 高致病性禽流感 (HPAI) 暴发 的模拟,探索生物医学、社会和经济专家在应对大流行病方面提供综合建议的潜力。此外,我们的目的是确定与高致病性禽流感大流行防范相关的知识和专业知识的跨领域差距。方法:我们基于源自荷兰且与儿童严重疾病相关的虚构 HPAI 暴发 进行了两次桌面模拟练习(2024 年 4 月/5 月)。共有 22 名和 19 名来自生物医学、社会和经济科学领域的专家参加。参与者首先在不同的生物医学和社会团队中起草了 暴发 管理建议,然后在混合小组中进行综合审议和建议。审议和预模拟访谈的书面记录用于归纳、反思性主题分析。结果:单独的咨询流程在紧迫性、情况评估以及起草的最佳和最坏情况方面有所不同。混合小组审议暴露了纪律盲点并促进了相互理解。特别是,由于观点相互矛盾,学校关闭问题引起了广泛讨论。在(基础)结构和指南的协调中确定了跨领域的知识和技术差距。结论:我们的模拟练习表明,综合咨询方法可能在克服大流行期间相互矛盾的建议方面具有附加值。需要进一步的研究来探索这种观察到的附加价值是否延伸到综合咨询机构。

analysis_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 该审查涉及 2024 年 4 月/5 月进行的两次桌面模拟练习,基于源自荷兰且与儿童严重疾病相关的虚构 HPAI 暴发。共有 22 名和 19 名来自生物医学、社会和经济科学领域的专家参加。使用归纳、反思性主题分析对审议和预模拟访谈的书面记录进行了分析。
analysis_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 模拟练习表明,综合咨询方法可能会在克服大流行期间相互冲突的建议方面提供附加值。混合小组审议暴露了纪律盲点并促进了相互理解,特别是在因观点冲突而关闭学校的问题上。在(基础)结构和指南的协调中确定了跨领域的知识和技术差距。
analysis_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 单独的咨询流程在紧迫性、情况评估以及起草的最佳和最坏情况方面有所不同。该研究强调需要进一步研究,以确定观察到的综合咨询的附加价值是否延伸到实际的综合咨询机构。
analysis_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 需要进一步研究来探索观察到的综合咨询的附加价值是否延伸到综合咨询机构。研究结果表明,跨学科调整(基础设施)结构和指南对于解决大流行病防范方面的知识差距非常重要。

papers.title: Predicting the Risk of Avian Influenza Zoonosis using Viral Genome Sequencing Data
papers.abstract: Abstract Avian Influenza viruses (AIVs) infect a broad host range despite having a natural reservoir in wild aquatic birds. Whilst most strains stay within their host species, some break the species barrier through genetic adaptations. We are most concerned about zoonotic cases, where a human becomes infected. Despite these events being rare, they are associated with high mortality and introduce the risk of onward human-to-human transmission of AIV. As a novel pathogen within the human population, this could have pandemic potential. Using genetic composition features for 8 AIV proteins drawn from viral sequence data, we employ machine-learning algorithms to classify AIV cases as zoonotic or not. These genetic features encode host ‘signatures’ which can indicate zoonosis and include frequency measures such as dipeptide composition and amino acid physiochemical properties. We consistently find XGBoost to outperform all other algorithms. We optimise parameters for ten classification models: one for each of the 8 proteins and two combined models. Following this, we show that a multi-model approach gives the best performing prediction for AIV zoonosis. We have identified all 8 proteins as having a role in predicting zoonotic transmission. Of particular importance is the PB2 and HA proteins, with specific amino acid physiochemical properties such as charge, secondary structure and hydrophobicity amongst the most indicative features in our combined models. Our alignment-free computational study can identify AIV cases still within avian hosts which are genetically closest to zoonotic AIV cases, thereby identifying the cases most likely to cross the species barrier. In a resource limited environment, our model could be used to quickly identify high priority cases for further investigation. Key points XGBoost is the best performing machine learning algorithm for the binary classification task of identifying avian influenza cases as zoonotic or not. Our model suggests that all eight proteins we considered have a role in determining whether avian influenza cases have zoonotic potential or not. Genetic composition features of avian influenza proteins can encode information that can be used as zoonotic signatures. We have created a system that identifies high priority cases still within avian hosts that should be prioritised for further investigation.

papers.title_original: Predicting the Risk of Avian Influenza Zoonosis using Viral Genome Sequencing Data

analysis.research_question_and_background: Avian Influenza viruses (AIVs) circulate widely in wild aquatic birds but occasionally cross species barriers to infect humans, posing pandemic risks due to high mortality and potential for onward transmission. The study addresses the need for tools to predict which AIV cases are likely to cause zoonosis before human infection occurs.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study uses a computational, alignment-free approach to classify AIV cases as zoonotic or non-zoonotic based on genetic composition features of eight viral proteins. It employs machine-learning algorithms, including XGBoost, to build classification models optimized for each protein and combined models.
analysis.methods: The authors extracted genetic composition features from eight AIV proteins, including dipeptide composition and amino acid physiochemical properties such as charge, secondary structure, and hydrophobicity. Ten classification models were optimized: one for each protein and two combined models, with XGBoost identified as the best-performing algorithm.
analysis.main_results: The study consistently found XGBoost to outperform other algorithms in classifying AIV cases as zoonotic or not. All eight proteins were identified as having a role in predicting zoonotic transmission, with PB2 and HA proteins highlighted as particularly important based on specific amino acid physiochemical properties.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret the findings as demonstrating that genetic composition features of AIV proteins can encode zoonotic signatures, enabling prediction of zoonotic potential. The novelty lies in the multi-model approach and the identification of specific protein features, such as those in PB2 and HA, as key indicators.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The model can prioritize AIV cases within avian hosts that are genetically closest to zoonotic cases, enabling rapid identification of high-priority cases for further investigation in resource-limited settings. This approach may improve surveillance and risk assessment for potential zoonotic spillover events.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is computational and alignment-free, relying on genetic features rather than experimental validation of zoonotic potential. The evidence strength is moderate due to the absence of in vivo or clinical validation and potential limitations in generalizability to diverse AIV strains.

analysis.summary_en: This study develops a computational framework to predict the zoonotic potential of avian influenza A viruses (AIVs) using genetic features from eight viral proteins. By employing machine-learning algorithms, particularly XGBoost, the authors demonstrate that genetic composition features such as dipeptide composition and amino acid physiochemical properties can serve as zoonotic signatures. All eight proteins, especially PB2 and HA, were identified as key predictors of zoonotic transmission. The multi-model approach outperformed single-protein models, enabling the identification of high-priority AIV cases within avian hosts that are genetically closest to zoonotic cases. papers.title_zh: 使用病毒 基因组 测序数据预测 禽流感 人兽共患病 的风险
papers.source_body_en: Abstract Avian Influenza viruses (AIVs) infect a broad host range despite having a natural reservoir in wild aquatic birds. Whilst most strains stay within their host species, some break the species barrier through genetic adaptations. We are most concerned about zoonotic cases, where a human becomes infected. Despite these events being rare, they are associated with high mortality and introduce the risk of onward human-to-human transmission of AIV. As a novel pathogen within the human population, this could have pandemic potential. Using genetic composition features for 8 AIV proteins drawn from viral sequence data, we employ machine-learning algorithms to classify AIV cases as zoonotic or not. These genetic features encode host ‘signatures’ which can indicate zoonosis and include frequency measures such as dipeptide composition and amino acid physiochemical properties. We consistently find XGBoost to outperform all other algorithms. We optimise parameters for ten classification models: one for each of the 8 proteins and two combined models. Following this, we show that a multi-model approach gives the best performing prediction for AIV zoonosis. We have identified all 8 proteins as having a role in predicting zoonotic transmission. Of particular importance is the PB2 and HA proteins, with specific amino acid physiochemical properties such as charge, secondary structure and hydrophobicity amongst the most indicative features in our combined models. Our alignment-free computational study can identify AIV cases still within avian hosts which are genetically closest to zoonotic AIV cases, thereby identifying the cases most likely to cross the species barrier. In a resource limited environment, our model could be used to quickly identify high priority cases for further investigation. Key points XGBoost is the best performing machine learning algorithm for the binary classification task of identifying avian influenza cases as zoonotic or not. Our model suggests that all eight proteins we considered have a role in determining whether avian influenza cases have zoonotic potential or not. Genetic composition features of avian influenza proteins can encode information that can be used as zoonotic signatures. We have created a system that identifies high priority cases still within avian hosts that should be prioritised for further investigation.

papers.title: Multistability, chaos, and transient dynamics in an avian influenza mathematical model
papers.abstract: Abstract Influenza, commonly known as the flu, is a highly contagious respiratory infection that causes symptoms, such as cough, aches, and malaise in infected individuals. One important form of influenza A infection is avian influenza, caused by the H5N1 virus, which has been a concern since the late twentieth century due to its high mortality rate. Monitoring and controlling avian influenza is of great importance for public health issues due to its ability to infect other mammals and its potential risk for spillover to humans. Mathematical models capable of describing the dynamics of avian influenza have been proposed to explore the spread of the disease and adapt control measures to contain it. In this work, we analyze the dynamical behavior of an avian influenza model consisting of two coupled SI (susceptible-infected) models, one describing the bird population and the other the human population. Using the bird mortality rate as the control parameter and hysteresis-type bifurcation diagrams, we identify bistability over a wide parameter range. As this parameter increases, we observe a significant range of hyperchaos. Furthermore, we uncover and quantify transient chaos and boundary crises for a given set of parameter values. These findings contribute to a more detailed understanding of the non-linear dynamics that may arise in mathematical models of avian influenza transmission.

Monitoring and controlling avian influenza is of great importance for public health issues due to its ability to infect other mammals and its potential risk for spillover to humans. Mathematical models capable of describing the dynamics of avian influenza have been proposed to explore the spread of the disease and adapt control measures to contain it. In this work, we analyze the dynamical behavior of an avian influenza model consisting of two coupled SI (susceptible-infected) models, one describing the bird population and the other the human population. Using the bird mortality rate as the control parameter and hysteresis-type bifurcation diagrams, we identify bistability over a wide parameter range. As this parameter increases, we observe a significant range of hyperchaos. Furthermore, we uncover and quantify transient chaos and boundary crises for a given set of parameter values. These findings contribute to a more detailed understanding of the non-linear dynamics that may arise in mathematical models of avian influenza transmission.

papers.title: Newton Divided Difference Optimization for Fingerprint-Based Neural Virtual Screening against Avian Influenza A/H9N2
papers.abstract: Avian influenza A/H9N2 poses persistent zoonotic and veterinary threats, yet efficient computational tools for antiviral compound prioritization remain underdeveloped, particularly with respect to optimizer behavior in high-dimensional neural screening. This study proposes Newton Divided Difference (NDD) optimization, a lightweight positive diagonal curvature-aware training strategy, as a novel optimizer for fingerprint-based neural virtual screening against avian influenza A/H9N2, with the objective of evaluating its performance across aligned molecular fingerprint representations and chemically structured validation protocols. An aligned benchmark of 1,459 molecules consisting of 615 candidate active compounds and 844 decoys was represented by EState (79 features), PubChem (881 features), and Klekota–Roth (4,860 features) fingerprints, sharing identical molecule identities, labels, and split assignments. A fixed multilayer perceptron (MLP) classifier was trained with NDD and seven baseline optimizers under stratified, scaffold-key, and similarity-cluster split protocols across five repeated seeds. NDD achieved the highest descriptive ROC-AUC (Receiver Operating Characteriztic – Area Under the Curve) and PR-AUC (Precision-Recall Area Under the Curve) on Klekota–Roth fingerprints under scaffold-key and similarity-cluster protocols, and remained competitive under the stratified split with ROC-AUC of 0.9872. Architecture-sensitivity tests confirmed stable NDD performance across multiple network configurations, with ROC-AUC values ranging from 0.9876 to 0.9890. Compared with Hessian-free optimization, NDD reduced per-run runtime from approximately 50–54 seconds to approximately 8 seconds on Klekota–Roth under the same CPU-only configuration while achieving comparable ranking performance. The novelty of this work lies in the first systematic assessment of NDD for H9N2 neural virtual screening, demonstrating that positive diagonal curvature-aware scaling provides a practical, stable, and computationally efficient optimization alternative in sparse high-dimensional ligand-based screening settings, although external validation and prospective experimental confirmation remain necessary before practical antiviral prioritization.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 禽流感 A/H9N2 造成持续的人畜共患病和兽医威胁,但用于 抗病毒药物 化合物优先级排序的有效计算工具仍然不发达,特别是在高维神经筛选中的​​优化器行为方面。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 本研究提出牛顿差分(NDD)优化作为一种​​针对 禽流感 A/H9N2 的基于指纹的神经虚拟筛选的新型优化器,目的是评估其在对齐的分子指纹表示和化学结构验证协议中的性能。
elements_zh.methods: 由 615 种候选活性化合物和 844 种诱饵组成的 1,459 个分子的对齐基准由 EState(79 个特征)、PubChem(881 个特征)和 Klekota–Roth(4,860 个特征)指纹代表,共享相同的分子身份、标签和分割分配。固定多层感知器 (MLP) 分类器使用 NDD 和七个基线优化器在分层、支架键和相似性聚类分割协议下跨五个重复种子进行训练。
elements_zh.main_results: NDD 在支架关键和相似性聚类协议下在 Klekota–Roth 指纹上实现了最高的描述性 ROC-AUC 和 PR-AUC,并且在分层分割下保持竞争力,ROC-AUC 为 0.9872。架构敏感性测试证实了跨多种网络配置的稳定 NDD 性能,ROC-AUC 值范围为 0.9876 至 0.9890。与无 Hessian 优化相比,在相同的仅 CPU 配置下,NDD 将 Klekota-Roth 上的每次运行时间从大约 50-54 秒减少到大约 8 秒,同时实现了相当的排名性能。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 这项工作的新颖性在于首次对 H9N2 神经虚拟筛选的 NDD 进行系统评估,证明正对角线曲率感知缩放在基于稀疏高维配体的筛选设置中提供了实用、稳定且计算高效的优化替代方案。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现为针对 禽流感 A/H9N2 的 抗病毒药物 化合物优先排序提供了一种计算有效的优化策略,这可以加速针对这种人畜共患威胁的潜在治疗方法的发现。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 在实施实际的 抗病毒药物 优先级排序之前,外部验证和前瞻性实验确认仍然是必要的。由于研究的计算性质和实验验证的需要,证据强度中等。

analysis_en.research_question_and_background: Avian influenza A/H9N2 poses persistent zoonotic and veterinary threats, yet efficient computational tools for antiviral compound prioritization remain underdeveloped, particularly with respect to optimizer behavior in high-dimensional neural screening.
analysis_en.study_design_and_population: This study proposes Newton Divided Difference (NDD) optimization as a novel optimizer for fingerprint-based neural virtual screening against avian influenza A/H9N2, with the objective of evaluating its performance across aligned molecular fingerprint representations and chemically structured validation protocols.
analysis_en.methods: An aligned benchmark of 1,459 molecules consisting of 615 candidate active compounds and 844 decoys was represented by EState (79 features), PubChem (881 features), and Klekota–Roth (4,860 features) fingerprints, sharing identical molecule identities, labels, and split assignments. A fixed multilayer perceptron (MLP) classifier was trained with NDD and seven baseline optimizers under stratified, scaffold-key, and similarity-cluster split protocols across five repeated seeds.
analysis_en.main_results: NDD achieved the highest descriptive ROC-AUC and PR-AUC on Klekota–Roth fingerprints under scaffold-key and similarity-cluster protocols, and remained competitive under the stratified split with ROC-AUC of 0.9872. Architecture-sensitivity tests confirmed stable NDD performance across multiple network configurations, with ROC-AUC values ranging from 0.9876 to 0.9890. Compared with Hessian-free optimization, NDD reduced per-run runtime from approximately 50–54 seconds to approximately 8 seconds on Klekota–Roth under the same CPU-only configuration while achieving comparable ranking performance.
analysis_en.interpretation_and_novelty: The novelty of this work lies in the first systematic assessment of NDD for H9N2 neural virtual screening, demonstrating that positive diagonal curvature-aware scaling provides a practical, stable, and computationally efficient optimization alternative in sparse high-dimensional ligand-based screening settings.
analysis_en.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings provide a computationally efficient optimization strategy for antiviral compound prioritization against avian influenza A/H9N2, which could accelerate the discovery of potential therapeutics for this zoonotic threat.
analysis_en.limitations_and_evidence_strength: External validation and prospective experimental confirmation remain necessary before practical antiviral prioritization can be implemented. The evidence strength is moderate due to the computational nature of the study and the need for experimental validation.

papers.title_zh: 针对 禽流感 A/H9N2 基于指纹的神经虚拟筛选的牛顿差分优化
papers.source_body_en: Avian influenza A/H9N2 poses persistent zoonotic and veterinary threats, yet efficient computational tools for antiviral compound prioritization remain underdeveloped, particularly with respect to optimizer behavior in high-dimensional neural screening. This study proposes Newton Divided Difference (NDD) optimization, a lightweight positive diagonal curvature-aware training strategy, as a novel optimizer for fingerprint-based neural virtual screening against avian influenza A/H9N2, with the objective of evaluating its performance across aligned molecular fingerprint representations and chemically structured validation protocols. An aligned benchmark of 1,459 molecules consisting of 615 candidate active compounds and 844 decoys was represented by EState (79 features), PubChem (881 features), and Klekota–Roth (4,860 features) fingerprints, sharing identical molecule identities, labels, and split assignments. A fixed multilayer perceptron (MLP) classifier was trained with NDD and seven baseline optimizers under stratified, scaffold-key, and similarity-cluster split protocols across five repeated seeds. NDD achieved the highest descriptive ROC-AUC (Receiver Operating Characteriztic – Area Under the Curve) and PR-AUC (Precision-Recall Area Under the Curve) on Klekota–Roth fingerprints under scaffold-key and similarity-cluster protocols, and remained competitive under the stratified split with ROC-AUC of 0.9872. Architecture-sensitivity tests confirmed stable NDD performance across multiple network configurations, with ROC-AUC values ranging from 0.9876 to 0.9890. Compared with Hessian-free optimization, NDD reduced per-run runtime from approximately 50–54 seconds to approximately 8 seconds on Klekota–Roth under the same CPU-only configuration while achieving comparable ranking performance. The novelty of this work lies in the first systematic assessment of NDD for H9N2 neural virtual screening, demonstrating that positive diagonal curvature-aware scaling provides a practical, stable, and computationally efficient optimization alternative in sparse high-dimensional ligand-based screening settings, although external validation and prospective experimental confirmation remain necessary before practical antiviral prioritization.

papers.title: Co-detection of highly pathogenic avian influenza A (H5N1) and SARS-CoV-2 in a bobcat ( Lynx rufus ), Washington, 2025
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Highly pathogenic avian influenza (HPAI) A(H5N1) and severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) are important One Health pathogens with expanding host ranges. We describe an investigation of a bobcat ( Lynx rufus ) in Washington State in which HPAI H5N1 clade 2.3.4.4b (genotype D1.1) and SARS-CoV-2 were co-detected. Clinical signs, diagnostic findings, and pathology were consistent with H5N1 infection. This report highlights the importance of integrated wildlife surveillance to characterize emerging zoonotic pathogens at the human-wildlife interface. IMPORTANCE This report documents the co-detection of two One Health threats, avian influenza and severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2, in a bobcat admitted to a wildlife rehabilitation facility. Although rare, the simultaneous detection of these viruses highlights gaps in routine monitoring of mammals and illustrates how wildlife may serve as bridging hosts for pathogens across the human-animal interface. Strengthening coordinated surveillance efforts is essential for understanding disease dynamics, protecting animal and public health, and supporting broader One Health preparedness strategies.

papers.source_body_en: ABSTRACT Highly pathogenic avian influenza (HPAI) A(H5N1) and severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) are important One Health pathogens with expanding host ranges. We describe an investigation of a bobcat ( Lynx rufus ) in Washington State in which HPAI H5N1 clade 2.3.4.4b (genotype D1.1) and SARS-CoV-2 were co-detected. Clinical signs, diagnostic findings, and pathology were consistent with H5N1 infection. This report highlights the importance of integrated wildlife surveillance to characterize emerging zoonotic pathogens at the human-wildlife interface. IMPORTANCE This report documents the co-detection of two One Health threats, avian influenza and severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2, in a bobcat admitted to a wildlife rehabilitation facility. Although rare, the simultaneous detection of these viruses highlights gaps in routine monitoring of mammals and illustrates how wildlife may serve as bridging hosts for pathogens across the human-animal interface. Strengthening coordinated surveillance efforts is essential for understanding disease dynamics, protecting animal and public health, and supporting broader One Health preparedness strategies.

papers.title: Surveillance without silos: a One Health data imperative for avian influenza in West Africa
papers.abstract: Highly pathogenic avian influenza (HPAI) has circulated in West Africa since Nigeria’s first human case in 2006, making the region a key entry point and dispersal hub for multiple virus lineages in sub-Saharan Africa. The 2.3.4.4b virus clade driving the global spread of avian influenza is now infecting mammals more often, a troubling sign that raises the risk of a future pandemic. At the same time, West Africa’s ability to control HPAI is held back by fragmented surveillance systems. Animal, human and environmental health services operate in isolation, rely on incompatible data formats and are managed by separate institutions, which undermines early detection and rapid response. This paper describes the existing surveillance silos in West Africa and outlines the consequences of failing to integrate them, including delayed detection of future human or animal health threats. It highlights emerging examples of One Health surveillance efforts in Nigeria, Senegal, Guinea, Benin and Ghana. From an operational standpoint, five conditions are essential for early warning and timely response: interoperable health information systems; shared governance across sectors; sustainable financing; strong communication with poultry-keeping communities; and effective cross-border collaboration. Establishing fully integrated, system-wide national surveillance platforms is indispensable for effective preparedness. Without such integration, West African countries will continue to detect and respond to emerging health threats too late. Given the region’s recurrent zoonotic spillover and expanding ecological vulnerabilities, embedding data integration at the core of preparedness strategies is essential for mitigating the risk of future pandemics.

papers.title_zh: 没有孤岛的 监测:西非 禽流感 的单一健康数据势在必行
papers.source_body_en: Highly pathogenic avian influenza (HPAI) has circulated in West Africa since Nigeria’s first human case in 2006, making the region a key entry point and dispersal hub for multiple virus lineages in sub-Saharan Africa. The 2.3.4.4b virus clade driving the global spread of avian influenza is now infecting mammals more often, a troubling sign that raises the risk of a future pandemic. At the same time, West Africa’s ability to control HPAI is held back by fragmented surveillance systems. Animal, human and environmental health services operate in isolation, rely on incompatible data formats and are managed by separate institutions, which undermines early detection and rapid response. This paper describes the existing surveillance silos in West Africa and outlines the consequences of failing to integrate them, including delayed detection of future human or animal health threats. It highlights emerging examples of One Health surveillance efforts in Nigeria, Senegal, Guinea, Benin and Ghana. From an operational standpoint, five conditions are essential for early warning and timely response: interoperable health information systems; shared governance across sectors; sustainable financing; strong communication with poultry-keeping communities; and effective cross-border collaboration. Establishing fully integrated, system-wide national surveillance platforms is indispensable for effective preparedness. Without such integration, West African countries will continue to detect and respond to emerging health threats too late. Given the region’s recurrent zoonotic spillover and expanding ecological vulnerabilities, embedding data integration at the core of preparedness strategies is essential for mitigating the risk of future pandemics.

papers.title: Genetic and Antigenic Characterization of a Clade 2.3.4.4b Highly Pathogenic H5N1 Avian Influenza Virus Isolated from a Free-Range Layer Duck in India
papers.abstract: Highly pathogenic avian influenza (HPAI) H5N1 virus poses a significant threat to the global poultry sector. The report highlights the genetic and antigenic features of a clade 2.3.4.4b HPAI H5N1 virus isolated from a free-range layer duck in the Kuttanad delta of Kerala, India, in 2022. The virus is similar to an H5N1 virus detected in Russia in October 2021 and antigenically distinct from clade 2.3.2, showing a 16-fold reduction in hemagglutination inhibition titer and 23.95% amino acid differences at the HA antigenic sites. The duck virus shares genetic similarities with H5N1 viruses found in Eurasian wild birds, suggesting a role for these birds in its introduction. The study underscores the importance of strengthening avian influenza surveillance to monitor virus evolution and spread.
papers.journal: Journal of Pure and Applied Microbiology

analysis.research_question_and_background: Highly pathogenic avian influenza (HPAI) H5N1 virus poses a significant threat to the global poultry sector. The study aimed to characterize a newly isolated HPAI H5N1 virus from a free-range layer duck in India.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study involved the isolation of a clade 2.3.4.4b HPAI H5N1 virus from a free-range layer duck in the Kuttanad delta of Kerala, India, in 2022. The virus was analyzed for its genetic and antigenic features.
analysis.methods: The virus was compared to an H5N1 virus detected in Russia in October 2021 and analyzed for antigenic differences. Genetic similarities with Eurasian wild bird H5N1 viruses were assessed to infer potential transmission routes.
analysis.main_results: The duck virus showed a 16-fold reduction in hemagglutination inhibition titer compared to clade 2.3.2 and had 23.95% amino acid differences at the HA antigenic sites. It shared genetic similarities with H5N1 viruses found in Eurasian wild birds.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings suggest that Eurasian wild birds may play a role in the introduction of this HPAI H5N1 virus into the duck population. This study provides new insights into the genetic and antigenic diversity of HPAI H5N1 viruses in India.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The study highlights the need for enhanced surveillance of avian influenza viruses to monitor their evolution and spread, which is crucial for preventing outbreaks in poultry and mitigating zoonotic risks.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is based on abstract-only evidence, which may limit the depth of analysis. However, the findings are grounded in direct comparisons of genetic and antigenic features, supporting a moderate confidence assessment.

analysis.summary_en: This study characterizes a clade 2.3.4.4b HPAI H5N1 virus isolated from a free-range layer duck in Kerala, India, in 2022. The virus exhibits genetic similarities with Eurasian wild bird H5N1 viruses, suggesting a possible role for these birds in its introduction. It also shows antigenic differences from clade 2.3.2, with a 16-fold reduction in hemagglutination inhibition titer and 23.95% amino acid variation at HA antigenic sites. The research underscores the importance of strengthening avian influenza surveillance to monitor virus evolution and spread, particularly in regions with free-range poultry. While the study is based on abstract-only evidence, the findings are supported by direct comparisons and provide moderate confidence in understanding the virus's characteristics and potential transmission routes.

elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究于 2022 年从印度喀拉拉邦库塔纳德三角洲的一只散养蛋鸭中分离出分支 2.3.4.4b HPAI H5N1 病毒。对该病毒的遗传和抗原特征进行了分析。
elements_zh.methods: 该病毒与 2021 年 10 月在俄罗斯检测到的 H5N1 病毒进行了比较,并分析了抗原差异。评估与欧亚 野生鸟类 H5N1 病毒的遗传相似性,以推断潜在的 传播 途径。
elements_zh.main_results: 与进化枝2.3.2相比,鸭病毒的血凝抑制滴度降低了16倍,并且HA抗原位点的氨基酸差异为23.95%。它与欧亚 野生鸟类 中发现的 H5N1 病毒具有遗传相似性。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究结果表明,欧亚 野生鸟类 可能在这种 HPAI H5N1 病毒引入鸭群的过程中发挥了作用。这项研究为印度 HPAI H5N1 病毒的遗传和抗原多样性提供了新的见解。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 该研究强调需要增强 禽流感 病毒的 监测 来监测其 进化 和传播,这对于在家禽中预防 暴发 和减轻人畜共患风险至关重要。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究仅基于抽象证据,这可能会限制分析的深度。然而,研究结果基于遗传和抗原特征的直接比较,支持适度的置信度评估。

papers.title_zh: 从印度散养蛋鸭中分离出的分支 2.3.4.4b 高致病性 H5N1 禽流感 病毒的遗传和抗原特征
papers.source_body_en: Highly pathogenic avian influenza (HPAI) H5N1 virus poses a significant threat to the global poultry sector. The report highlights the genetic and antigenic features of a clade 2.3.4.4b HPAI H5N1 virus isolated from a free-range layer duck in the Kuttanad delta of Kerala, India, in 2022. The virus is similar to an H5N1 virus detected in Russia in October 2021 and antigenically distinct from clade 2.3.2, showing a 16-fold reduction in hemagglutination inhibition titer and 23.95% amino acid differences at the HA antigenic sites. The duck virus shares genetic similarities with H5N1 viruses found in Eurasian wild birds, suggesting a role for these birds in its introduction. The study underscores the importance of strengthening avian influenza surveillance to monitor virus evolution and spread.

papers.title: H5N1 influenza multi-epitope vaccine design through immunoinformatics approaches
papers.abstract: The H5N1 avian influenza virus poses a significant threat to both animal and human health, with a high potential for triggering a global pandemic. This study outlines a step-by-step immunoinformatics-driven approach to design a multi-epitope vaccine against H5N1. Potential vaccine candidates were identified by analyzing the sequences of conserved H5N1 proteins, including Hemagglutinin, Neuraminidase, and Matrix protein 1 and 2. B-cell epitopes and T-cell peptides were predicted and then screened for toxicity and allergenicity. The final vaccine construct has been verified for structural stability and computer simulation has been used to evaluate its theoretical potential for eliciting a long-lasting immune response. This In silico approach leverages a suite of computational tools to accelerate vaccine design by prioritizing promising candidates for experimental validation.
papers.journal: Frontiers in Applied Mathematics and Statistics

While the approach demonstrates a step-by-step in silico pipeline, the findings rely solely on computational predictions without experimental or clinical validation, limiting their immediate applicability.

papers.title: The first high pathogenicity avian influenza A(H5N1) clade 2.3.4.4b incursions in the Hunter New England region, New South Wales, Australia, June–July 2026
papers.abstract: Two incursions of high pathogenicity avian influenza (HPAI) A(H5N1) clade 2.3.4.4b in vagrant birds were identified in the Hunter New England region of New South Wales, Australia on 28 June 2026 and 10 July 2026. These were the first detections of the virus in New South Wales and occurred shortly after the first Australian detection in June 2026. The Hunter New England Population Health Unit managed human contacts of the infected birds using a contact management system designed and purpose-built by the Unit. We report on the public health response and opportunities for improvement.

papers.title: Editorial: Sequencing technologies in advancing veterinary and zoonotic infection research
papers.abstract: Sequencing as a transformative frameworkInfectious disease threats are wide-ranging, global and interconnected, affecting livestock productivity and revenue, food security, wildlife conservation, and human health. Disease emergence and transmission are driven by ecological, environmental and anthropogenic factors, including animal movement and trade, agricultural intensification, inadequate biosecurity, climate change, and wildlifelivestock-human interfaces.Integration of genomic sequencing with epidemiological surveillance and appropriate metadata generates high-resolution, actionable information. Depending on the approach and analytical objective, outputs may include genome recovery and genotyping of causative agents, characterization of mixed and coinfections, identification of mutations, reassortment and recombination events, discovery of novel pathogens, and profiling of virulence determinants (Gardy and Loman, 2018;Armstrong et al., 2019). Sequencing approaches span a continuum suited to different questions, from targeted, highresolution characterization of known pathogens to broader, pathogen-agnostic discovery (Rong et al., 2026).The 16 papers assembled in this Research Topic collectively illustrate complementary roles of sequencing technologies across this continuum, from methodological optimization and diagnostic investigations to genomic surveillance, evolutionary analyses, and biological interpretation. Together, these studies demonstrate the expanding role of sequencing technologies in advancing veterinary and zoonotic infection research.Making sequencing faster, more accessible, and fit for purposeThe value of genomic sequencing depends on the entire workflow rather than the sequencing instrument alone. Because no workflow is universally optimal, methods should be selected according to the biological question or application, sample type and quality, expected pathogen abundance, genome characteristics, required throughput and turnaround time, and available computational resources (Berry et al., 2020). Target enrichment represents another important strategy for improving sequencing efficiency. Using avian metapneumovirus as a model, Álvarez-Narváez et al. showed that tiled amplicon-based sequencing substantially improved genome recovery from samples with high host background while remaining compatible with both short-and long-read platforms. Because this approach depends on prior sequence knowledge, continued surveillance and periodic primer updates are essential as viral populations continue to evolve.Finally, Kattoor et al. demonstrated that multiplex targeted sequencing can simultaneously detect multiple pathogens associated with canine neurological and reproductive diseases while providing strain-level information. Such syndromic approaches bridge the gap between conventional singletarget PCR and untargeted metagenomics, although expanding the number of targets may reduce analytical sensitivity and increase assay complexity.Pathogen-agnostic sequencing approaches complement hypothesis-driven diagnostic methods in investigations of unresolved, atypical, multifactorial or multi-agent infectious diseases. Untargeted metagenomic sequencing is hypothesis-free in target selection, but not interpretation-free, meaning that biological and clinical judgement are essential for distinguishing true pathogens from commensals, incidental detections, and background contaminants (Miller and Chiu, 2022).The untargeted metagenomic study by Kariithi et al. demonstrated the complexity of disease-associated viral communities through co-detection and genomic characterization of multiple genetically diverse enteric viruses in pooled poultry samples, revealing distinct genomic constellations and reassortmentrelated patterns. The study illustrates that metagenomic sequencing can comprehensively define complex viral communities. However, determining the relative contribution of individual pathogens to disease and establishing causality still require integration with clinical, pathological, and epidemiological evidence. Such approaches provide a more complete etiological picture and help prioritize candidate pathogens for subsequent investigations.Beyond pathogen detection alone, genomic sequences place outbreak-associated pathogens within their evolutionary context, enabling comparison with prevailing strains and strengthening epidemiological investigations (Robinson et al., 2013) In addition to identifying the causative agent, WGS can resolve genetic lineages, spatial and temporal clustering, reassortment and recombination events, transmission pathways, introduction into and persistence within local populations, and outbreak boundaries. Collectively, these capabilities provide the genomic context needed for surveillance and disease control decisions (Struelens et al., 2024).Because migratory birds, particularly waterfowl, are natural reservoirs of avian influenza viruses (Olsen et al., 2006), surveillance of wild birds provides an early warning system for detecting viruses with potential to be introduced into poultry and, in some cases, human populations. The report by Si et al. on H5N1 and H5N9 highly pathogenic avian influenza viruses demonstrated the value of sequencing at the beginning of migration by enabling early recognition of newly introduced lineages. It further identified complete gene constellations, reassortment patterns and mutations with potential implications for host range and pathogenicity, thereby informing surveillance, diagnostic, and risk assessment efforts.Even recovery of a single isolate can substantially expand genomic knowledge, particularly for rare or poorly characterized pathogens. The incidental detection and genomic characterization of the first coding-complete Avian orthoavulavirus 16 (AOAV-16) genome from a cinereous vulture by Son et al. during influenza surveillance extended the known host range beyond wild Anseriformes, the avian order in which the virus has predominantly been detected. Considering the scarcity of AOAV -16 genomic resources, such reports expand reference databases, which are critical for whole-genomebased classifications, and improve understanding of the host range and geographical distribution of AOAV-16.Beyond expanding genomic resources for rare viruses, WGS also strengthens genomic epidemiology of zoonotic bacterial pathogens. This is illustrated by Yang Qiuju et al., who characterized the first reported human isolate of Brucella canis using comparative genomics and whole-genome SNP analysis, thereby clarifying its phylogenetic relationships and highlighting the need for enhanced surveillance. Similarly, Yang Yong et al. used integrated genomic analyses of B. abortus isolates from humans and cattle to define their population structure, phylogenetic relationships, and regional transmission patterns, illustrating how WGS strengthens surveillance and source attribution of important zoonotic bacteria.Beyond identifying and tracking pathogens, genomic sequencing can provide important insights into biological characteristics and host-pathogen interactions. However, genomic datasets predict biological potential rather than expressed phenotype or disease outcome. Their interpretation therefore requires integration with complementary laboratory, pathological, and epidemiological evidence (Balloux et al., 2018;Sheppard et al., 2018).In their study of avian pathogenic Escherichia coli O145, Tan et al. combined WGS, experimental infection, pathology, and in vivo transcriptomics to investigate pathogenicity and host adaptation.Transcriptomic comparison of bacteria colonizing duck liver with those grown in vitro identified 87 differentially expressed genes, including genes associated with metabolism and host adaptation, as well as changes in central metabolic pathways and regulatory small RNAs. The study illustrates how genomic potential can be linked to genes and pathways expressed under specific host conditions, although the biological functions of many identified transcripts remain to be experimentally validated.Wang et al. further demonstrated that multidimensional characterization of newly detected lineages benefits from the integration of genomic and phenotypic analyses. Hybrid WGS defined the phylogenetic placement, resistome, virulome, and mobile genetic elements of the novel Acinetobacter baumannii ST3475 lineage, whereas cell-based assays and animal models demonstrated enhanced biofilm formation, adhesion, invasion and pathogenicity. Although phylogenetic clustering suggested possible adaptation to the bovine mammary niche, broader surveillance and epidemiological investigations are needed to determine its zoonotic potential.Finally, Mohamed et al. synthesized evidence on virulence-associated genes in Campylobacter jejuni and C. coli from food and human sources across Gulf Cooperation Council countries. The review highlighted heterogeneous virulence profiles and important regional evidence gaps, particularly the limited number of human studies and uncertainty surrounding the relationship between gene carriage and pathogenicity. Such regional syntheses can support the development of harmonized surveillance strategies and help prioritize virulence determinants for functional investigation.The studies published in this Research Topic collectively demonstrate how sequencing has evolved beyond pathogen detection into a versatile platform supporting diagnostics, pathogen discovery, outbreak investigation, epidemiological surveillance, comparative genomics, and functional investigations. Across diverse pathogens and host species, sequencing consistently provided greater resolution than conventional diagnostic approaches while expanding understanding of pathogen diversity, evolution, and biology.An equally important lesson emerging from this collection is that genomic data are most valuable when interpreted alongside complementary clinical, pathological, phenotypic and epidemiological evidence. Likewise, the methodological studies demonstrate that successful implementation depends not only on sequencing technologies but also on optimized workflows tailored to specific diagnostic, surveillance , and research applications. These findings underscore the importance of matching sequencing strategies, analytical methods, and validation approaches to the intended application.Taken together, these studies reflect the continuing transition of sequencing from a specialized research tool to an increasingly accessible platform supporting veterinary and zoonotic infectious disease investigations. Continued progress will require optimized, standardized workflows, integration of genomic data with complementary biological and epidemiological evidence, sustained genomic surveillance, and multidisciplinary collaboration within a One Health framework. These priorities will be essential for strengthening infectious disease preparedness, detection and response to both existing and emerging disease threats.

However, genomic datasets predict biological potential rather than expressed phenotype or disease outcome. Continued progress will require optimized, standardized workflows, integration of genomic data with complementary biological and epidemiological evidence, sustained genomic surveillance, and multidisciplinary collaboration within a One Health framework. These priorities will be essential for strengthening infectious disease preparedness, detection and response to both existing and emerging disease threats.
