analysis_en.scale_impact_and_risk: Nationwide: 297 confirmed H5N1 cases as of August 22, 2026; >1,000 greater crested terns and >24 little penguins killed; silver gull positive in early August. Risk: Feeder-created hotspots may accelerate spread to agricultural zones and urban areas; mammals (e.g., possums, foxes, Tasmanian devils, quolls, kangaroos, wallabies) face exposure via scavenging infected bird carcasses. Human risk remains low; no human infections detected in Australia.
analysis_en.response_status_and_uncertainty: CSIRO's Australian Centre for Disease Preparedness confirmed the diagnosis. Authorities acknowledge inability to avoid significant losses once H5N1 spreads in the environment. No evidence yet of broader marine mammal outbreak. Public urged to stop or modify bird feeding; research indicates birds derive <10% of diet from feeders, mitigating harm from cessation. Wildlife carers and veterinarians advised to follow biosafety protocols. Extinction risk highlighted for critically endangered species like the orange-bellied parrot.

news.title_zh: 澳大利亚大陆首例哺乳动物死亡后,后院喂鸟器导致 H5N1 病毒传播 - 科技时报
news.source_body_en: Australia confirmed its first mainland mammal death from H5N1 avian influenza on August 23, 2026, after a long-nosed fur seal tested positive near Beachport, South Australia. The case, verified by CSIRO, follows a rapid escalation of H5N1 detections nationwide, including 297 confirmed cases and mass mortalities among seabirds such as greater crested terns and little penguins. Researchers warn that backyard bird feeders are inadvertently creating transmission hotspots by concentrating multiple bird species at unnaturally high densities, accelerating viral spread into new species and environments. While human risk remains low with no local infections reported, mammals—including possums, foxes, and Tasmanian devils—face elevated exposure through scavenging infected carcasses. Authorities urge the public to cease or modify bird feeding, citing evidence that wild birds derive less than 10% of their diet from feeders, minimizing harm to avian populations. The outbreak also threatens critically endangered species like the orange-bellied parrot, raising extinction risks.

news.content: CHINAGLOBAL EDITION HONG KONG HOME NEWS Hong Kong Nation Asia World Business Science Sports FOCUS Life & Art In-depth China Quirky Photo Graphics Data Culture HK Global Weekly Eye on Asia Special From PR Newswire OPINION Editorials Columnists Joephy Chan Bill Condon David Cottam Grenville Cross Richard Cullen Dong Yu Michael Edesess Wilson Lee Flores Tom Fowdy Fu Kin-chi Henry Ho Ho Lok-sang Ken Ip Regina Ip Tony Kwok Lau Siu-kai Dominic Lee Virginia Lee Liu Ningrong Christine Loh James Ockenden Quentin Parker Tu Haiming Xiao Ping Roy Ying GBA GBA Guide GBA Life GBA in Figures GBA Pulse VIDEO News Asia Featured CDHK In-Depth China Daily DOCS Drone and Phone Girl City Peak Talk Tech Asia The Gold ADVANCED NEWS> Asia> Content> Published: 03:00, August 24, 2026 South Australia reports 2nd suspected mammal bird flu case in seal By Xinhua Share This undated electron microscopic image provided by the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention shows two Influenza A (H5N1) virions, a type of bird flu virus. (PHOTO/CDC VIA AP) CANBERRA – South Australian authorities on Monday reported a second suspected case of H5N1 bird flu in a seal, one day after the state reported Australia's first case in a mammal. South Australia's Department of Primary Industries and Regions said on Monday that the long-nosed fur seal was found at the Pages Conservation Park, a protected area consisting of the North Page and South Page islands located about 18 km off the state's south coast. The department said that samples have been sent to the Australian Center for Disease Preparedness for confirmatory testing. It comes after the federal government on Sunday announced that Australia's first confirmed case of the highly pathogenic H5N1 avian influenza strain in a mammal had been confirmed in a long-nosed fur seal found dead in mainland South Australia on Wednesday. ALSO READ: Australia confirms first H5 bird flu case in mammal South Australian Minister for Climate, Environment and Water Emily Bourke said that the two cases were incredibly concerning. The state government on Thursday said that over 1,000 birds had been found dead in suspected H5N1 mass mortality events on three islands, including North Page and South Page. "We've seen devastation in seals around the world when it comes to bird flu," Bourke told Australian Broadcasting Corporation (ABC) radio on Monday. According to the National Parks and Wildlife Service, the Page islands are home to one of three large colonies of endangered Australian sea lions in South Australia. The Invasive Species Council has warned that the H5N1 outbreak could be an extinction-level event for the species. READ MORE: Australia confirms first mass death of seabirds from H5N1 bird flu Bourke said that the strain circulating in South Australia potentially arrived in the state from Heard Island, a remote sub-Antarctic Australian territory. The Australian Antarctic Program said in June that around 13,000 of the estimated 17,000 elephant seal pups on Heard Island had died from H5N1 avian influenza. Federal Minister for the Environment and Water Murray Watt told ABC television on Monday that the cases in seals were not unexpected and authorities expect to see more mass mortality events. news.source_body_en: South Australia has reported a second suspected case of H5N1 bird flu in a long-nosed fur seal, following the first confirmed case in a mammal. The seal was found at Pages Conservation Park, a protected area off the state's south coast. The Department of Primary Industries and Regions confirmed the suspected case, with samples sent for confirmatory testing. Over 1,000 birds have been found dead in suspected H5N1 mass mortality events on three islands, including North Page and South Page. The outbreak has raised concerns about potential extinction-level events for the species. The federal government and state authorities are monitoring the situation, with the minister for the environment noting that the cases were not unexpected and more events are expected. The H5N1 strain may have originated from Heard Island, where around 13,000 elephant seal pups died from the virus in June. The outbreak highlights the growing threat of avian influenza to marine mammals and ecosystems.

Innovation Live H5N1 Was Isolated from Fetal Bovine Serum in a Finding That Puts Laboratory Biosafety Under New Scrutiny Published Aug 24, 2026 6:30 AM EDT By Cole Mercer LUIS ROBAYO | AFP via Getty Images Share on Twitter Share on Facebook Share on Pocket Researchers at Cornell University isolated live, infectious H5N1 avian influenza virus from a commercial lot of fetal bovine serum, the growth supplement used in cell culture laboratories worldwide, in a report published in the August issue of the CDC journal Emerging Infectious Diseases. The finding matters to a specific audience, and it is worth stating plainly who that is. This is a laboratory biosafety and manufacturing quality-control story, not a consumer exposure story. No pasteurized dairy product, retail meat item, or medical treatment is implicated. The people whose practices may change are diagnosticians, cell culture technicians, biomanufacturing staff, and the institutional biosafety committees that write their protocols. The detection also carries one immediately reassuring result. Heating the serum to 56 degrees Celsius for 30 minutes, a step already built into many commercial serum products and lab protocols, inactivated the virus in the authors' experiments. Routine Screening at Cornell Caught the Contaminated Lot The lot arrived at the Virology Laboratory of the Cornell Animal Health Diagnostic Center in February 2025 for routine extraneous agents testing, a screening requirement under federal regulations governing biological products of animal origin. It was not submitted because anyone suspected contamination. Sequencing identified the virus as highly pathogenic avian influenza A(H5N1) clade 2.3.4.4b, genotype B3.13, the lineage that has been circulating in U.S. dairy cattle since March 2024. As of mid-December 2025, more than 1,084 herds in 19 states had been affected, with most concentrated in California. The tested lot was a pool of samples collected in five states: Pennsylvania, Kansas, Nebraska, South Carolina, and California. That detail is the load-bearing one for anyone assessing risk in their own supply chain, and it is addressed below. Serum Is a Pooled Product, and That Matters Fetal bovine serum is collected from bovine fetuses at slaughterhouses and is, in the paper's own framing, the most frequently used growth supplement in cell culture media. It is commonly added to basal media at concentrations of about 5-10% and supports a wide range of cell types in academic research, pharmaceutical development, and biomanufacturing. Because it is pooled from many animals, a single infected donor can contribute a large amount that is subsequently widely distributed. The Cornell team followed the positive lot with broader testing, screening individual serum samples collected at slaughterhouses in California and Texas, 384 from each state. Of those 768 samples, one tested positive by real-time reverse transcription PCR, at a cycle threshold of 35, indicating a low viral load. The authors interpret that pattern as consistent with sporadic viremia in infected lactating dairy cattle, allowing the virus to reach tissues beyond the udder, including, on rare occasions, the fetus. Follow-up testing of 13 additional bottles from the same original lot, eight of them not heat-inactivated and five heat-inactivated, is documented in a summary table accompanying the paper, using virus isolation in two cell lines, embryonated eggs, and PCR. Detection was infrequent even by PCR, and attempts to confirm virus isolation at USDA's National Veterinary Services Laboratories were not successful, which the authors take as evidence of very low viral loads in the pooled lot. Heat Treatment Cleared the Virus in Laboratory Tests The inactivation experiment is the part with an actionable conclusion. Serum aliquots were spiked with bovine H5N1 at high titer and heated. The authors report that heating at 56 degrees Celsius for 30 minutes inactivated the virus, and they conclude that although finding a zoonotic virus in serum raises biosafety concerns for diagnostic testing of bovine serum and for laboratory procedures using it, "heat treatment of FBS seems to be efficient in inactivating the virus" and could serve as a safety precaution. That temperature and duration are not novel. Commercial suppliers, including ATCC, publish 56 degrees for 30 minutes as the standard heat-inactivation protocol, and heat-inactivated serum is sold as a distinct product line. The complication is that heat inactivation is not a universal practice because suppliers caution that it is unnecessary for many cell lines and can degrade heat-labile growth factors that some cells require. The result also aligns with earlier work. Heat inactivation of H5N1 in raw cow's milk was examined in a report in the New England Journal of Medicine, part of a broader body of research into how thermal treatment affects this virus in bovine-origin material. Consumers Are Not the Audience for This Finding Several limitations go hand in hand with the headline result. This is a single documented lot, identified through routine surveillance rather than through any adverse event. No laboratory-acquired infection has been reported in connection with it. The authors note that their findings and conclusions do not necessarily reflect the official positions of the agencies involved, and that one co-author is affiliated with USDA's Animal and Plant Health Inspection Service. The paper does not establish how often serum lots are contaminated because it was not designed to. Nor does it demonstrate that anyone has been infected through this route. It documents that a live virus survived in a commercial biological product and that a widely available treatment step neutralized it under laboratory conditions. What laboratories and biomanufacturers may reasonably reconsider is whether their current serum sourcing, screening, and heat-treatment decisions account for a pathogen that was not circulating in U.S. cattle three years ago. Institutional biosafety committees, not individual bench scientists, are typically the right level for that review. Facilities working with bovine-origin material should confirm what their supplier tests for and whether their lots are heat-inactivated. The broader surveillance question remains open. Continued monitoring of H5N1 in dairy cattle and of the animal-origin products the herds feed into is tracked through the CDC journal's influenza research collection. Whether contamination of serum proves to be rare or more common than a single lot suggests will depend on testing that has not yet been reported. Read more China Reports Four More H9N2 Infections as U.S. Bird Flu Risk Stays Low for the General Public H5N1 Bird Flu Has Now Hit Over 1,166 U.S. Dairy Herds Across 19 States, With Idaho Leading the Nation More Than 100 Experts Say Ending PAHO Funding Would Weaken Early Warning for Diseases Reaching U.S. Farms Key Questions Answered What did researchers find? Live, infectious H5N1 avian influenza virus was isolated from a commercial lot of fetal bovine serum submitted to the Cornell Animal Health Diagnostic Center for routine screening. Sequencing identified genotype B3.13. Is this a risk to consumers? No consumer product is implicated. Fetal bovine serum is a laboratory and biomanufacturing reagent, not a food ingredient, and the report concerns laboratory biosafety rather than dietary exposure. Did anyone get sick from it? No laboratory-acquired infection has been reported in connection with this lot. The detection came from routine testing, not from an illness investigation. Does heat treatment solve the problem? In these experiments, heating serum to 56 degrees Celsius for 30 minutes inactivated the virus. That protocol is already standard for heat-inactivated serum products, though heat inactivation is not used for every cell line. How could a virus reach a fetal sample? The authors suggest sporadic bloodstream infection in lactating dairy cattle can allow the virus to reach tissues beyond the udder, including, in rare cases, the fetus. How common is contamination? Unknown. The study documents one positive lot and one positive individual sample among 768 samples tested at slaughterhouses in two states. It was not designed to estimate overall prevalence. Who should act on this? Institutional biosafety committees, diagnostic laboratories and biomanufacturers using bovine-origin material, who may want to confirm supplier testing and heat-treatment status for their serum lots. Innovation Live H5N1 Was Isolated from Fetal Bovine Serum in a Finding That Puts Laboratory Biosafety Under New Scrutiny Published Aug 24, 2026 6:30 AM EDT By Cole Mercer LUIS ROBAYO | AFP via Getty Images Share on Twitter Share on Facebook Share on Pocket Researchers at Cornell University isolated live, infectious H5N1 avian influenza virus from a commercial lot of fetal bovine serum, the growth supplement used in cell culture laboratories worldwide, in a report published in the August issue of the CDC journal Emerging Infectious Diseases. The finding matters to a specific audience, and it is worth stating plainly who that is. This is a laboratory biosafety and manufacturing quality-control story, not a consumer exposure story. No pasteurized dairy product, retail meat item, or medical treatment is implicated. The people whose practices may change are diagnosticians, cell culture technicians, biomanufacturing staff, and the institutional biosafety committees that write their protocols. The detection also carries one immediately reassuring result. Heating the serum to 56 degrees Celsius for 30 minutes, a step already built into many commercial serum products and lab protocols, inactivated the virus in the authors' experiments. Routine Screening at Cornell Caught the Contaminated Lot The lot arrived at the Virology Laboratory of the Cornell Animal Health Diagnostic Center in February 2025 for routine extraneous agents testing, a screening requirement under federal regulations governing biological products of animal origin. It was not submitted because anyone suspected contamination. Sequencing identified the virus as highly pathogenic avian influenza A(H5N1) clade 2.3.4.4b, genotype B3.13, the lineage that has been circulating in U.S. dairy cattle since March 2024. As of mid-December 2025, more than 1,084 herds in 19 states had been affected, with most concentrated in California. The tested lot was a pool of samples collected in five states: Pennsylvania, Kansas, Nebraska, South Carolina, and California. That detail is the load-bearing one for anyone assessing risk in their own supply chain, and it is addressed below. Serum Is a Pooled Product, and That Matters Fetal bovine serum is collected from bovine fetuses at slaughterhouses and is, in the paper's own framing, the most frequently used growth supplement in cell culture media. It is commonly added to basal media at concentrations of about 5-10% and supports a wide range of cell types in academic research, pharmaceutical development, and biomanufacturing. Because it is pooled from many animals, a single infected donor can contribute a large amount that is subsequently widely distributed. The Cornell team followed the positive lot with broader testing, screening individual serum samples collected at slaughterhouses in California and Texas, 384 from each state. Of those 768 samples, one tested positive by real-time reverse transcription PCR, at a cycle threshold of 35, indicating a low viral load. The authors interpret that pattern as consistent with sporadic viremia in infected lactating dairy cattle, allowing the virus to reach tissues beyond the udder, including, on rare occasions, the fetus. Follow-up testing of 13 additional bottles from the same original lot, eight of them not heat-inactivated and five heat-inactivated, is documented in a summary table accompanying the paper, using virus isolation in two cell lines, embryonated eggs, and PCR. Detection was infrequent even by PCR, and attempts to confirm virus isolation at USDA's National Veterinary Services Laboratories were not successful, which the authors take as evidence of very low viral loads in the pooled lot. Heat Treatment Cleared the Virus in Laboratory Tests The inactivation experiment is the part with an actionable conclusion. Serum aliquots were spiked with bovine H5N1 at high titer and heated. The authors report that heating at 56 degrees Celsius for 30 minutes inactivated the virus, and they conclude that although finding a zoonotic virus in serum raises biosafety concerns for diagnostic testing of bovine serum and for laboratory procedures using it, "heat treatment of FBS seems to be efficient in inactivating the virus" and could serve as a safety precaution. That temperature and duration are not novel. Commercial suppliers, including ATCC, publish 56 degrees for 30 minutes as the standard heat-inactivation protocol, and heat-inactivated serum is sold as a distinct product line. The complication is that heat inactivation is not a universal practice because suppliers caution that it is unnecessary for many cell lines and can degrade heat-labile growth factors that some cells require. The result also aligns with earlier work. Heat inactivation of H5N1 in raw cow's milk was examined in a report in the New England Journal of Medicine, part of a broader body of research into how thermal treatment affects this virus in bovine-origin material. Consumers Are Not the Audience for This Finding Several limitations go hand in hand with the headline result. This is a single documented lot, identified through routine surveillance rather than through any adverse event. No laboratory-acquired infection has been reported in connection with it. The authors note that their findings and conclusions do not necessarily reflect the official positions of the agencies involved, and that one co-author is affiliated with USDA's Animal and Plant Health Inspection Service. The paper does not establish how often serum lots are contaminated because it was not designed to. Nor does it demonstrate that anyone has been infected through this route. It documents that a live virus survived in a commercial biological product and that a widely available treatment step neutralized it under laboratory conditions. What laboratories and biomanufacturers may reasonably reconsider is whether their current serum sourcing, screening, and heat-treatment decisions account for a pathogen that was not circulating in U.S. cattle three years ago. Institutional biosafety committees, not individual bench scientists, are typically the right level for that review. Facilities working with bovine-origin material should confirm what their supplier tests for and whether their lots are heat-inactivated. The broader surveillance question remains open. Continued monitoring of H5N1 in dairy cattle and of the animal-origin products the herds feed into is tracked through the CDC journal's influenza research collection. Whether contamination of serum proves to be rare or more common than a single lot suggests will depend on testing that has not yet been reported. Live, infectious H5N1 avian influenza virus was isolated from a commercial lot of fetal bovine serum submitted to the Cornell Animal Health Diagnostic Center for routine screening. Sequencing identified genotype B3.13. Is this a risk to consumers? No consumer product is implicated. Fetal bovine serum is a laboratory and biomanufacturing reagent, not a food ingredient, and the report concerns laboratory biosafety rather than dietary exposure. Did anyone get sick from it? No laboratory-acquired infection has been reported in connection with this lot. The detection came from routine testing, not from an illness investigation. Does heat treatment solve the problem? In these experiments, heating serum to 56 degrees Celsius for 30 minutes inactivated the virus. That protocol is already standard for heat-inactivated serum products, though heat inactivation is not used for every cell line. How could a virus reach a fetal sample? The authors suggest sporadic bloodstream infection in lactating dairy cattle can allow the virus to reach tissues beyond the udder, including, in rare cases, the fetus. How common is contamination? Unknown. The study documents one positive lot and one positive individual sample among 768 samples tested at slaughterhouses in two states. It was not designed to estimate overall prevalence. Who should act on this? Institutional biosafety committees, diagnostic laboratories and biomanufacturers using bovine-origin material, who may want to confirm supplier testing and heat-treatment status for their serum lots. Thursday, August 27, 2026 UK National Risk Register 2026 - Urges Citizen Preparedness #19,311 In August of 2008 we looked at the first UK National Risk Register - which ran just 52 pages - and cited pandemic flu as the #1 threat facing the nation. It's prep advice to the public was fairly limited, essentially urging: Creating a core stock of essential supplies. This could include bottled water, a battery powered radio, torch, tinned food and alternative heating sources. Four years later, a slightly larger (58 page) 2012 update was released, which kept pandemic flu at the top of their threat board, but added coastal flooding, terrorist attacks, severe space weather, prolonged power or gas outages, and even volcanic threats to the list. The last time we looked at the UK Risk Register was in August of 2023, which by that time has expanded to nearly 200 pages. Partners with AgriNerds to Create First-of-its-Kind, Dynamic Avian Influenza Surveillance System for U.S. Poultry Farmers [August 25, 2026] Alveo Technologies Partners with AgriNerds to Create First-of-its-Kind, Dynamic Avian Influenza Surveillance System for U.S. Poultry Farmers Tweet Linking on-site, rapid molecular HPAI testing to real-time HPAI modeling of migratory birds to help farmers run dynamic, risk-informed surveillance programs ALAMEDA, Calif., Aug. 25, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Alveo Technologies, Inc., a global leader in rapid, point-of-need molecular diagnostics for early disease detection, today announced a strategic partnership with AgriNerds Inc, which has developed the Waterfowl Alert Network, a first-of-its-kind dynamic surveillance and awareness program that predicts historic and daily waterfowl activity around the nation's poultry and livestock farms. The partnership will pair Alveo's unique, rapid, molecular diagnostic with AgriNerds' Waterfowl Alert Network, a proprietary system that uses a combination of satellite imagery, weather radar, and telemetry to create daily farm-level HPAI risk scores based on remote sensing and HPAI surveillance data. To defend against HPAI and other pathogens, poultry producers have heavily invested in strengthening their biosecurity programs, but farms continue to suffer from HPAI outbreaks triggered by migratory birds, which is the source of infection for 68% of US H5N1 outbreaks since 2022, according to the APHIS. Currenty, producers typically take one of two strategies for testing. Most test only when animals display flu-like symptoms, but this approach risks detecting the virus too late to prevent it from spreading. Some conduct periodic blind surveillance testing, which has the advantage of enabling early detection, but can be expensive. Alveo and AgriNerds are partnering to develop a new rapid and targeted approach: dynamic surveillance that alerts farmers when the risk of infection is high. AgriNerds' Waterfowl Alert Network will use radar imagery to detect migratory bird movements, analyze the data using AI-powered pattern recognition software, and generate daily risk scores it shares with customers. When risk escalates, Alveo's on-farm molecular test will help farms to conduct asymptomatic surveillance testing that provides precise results in under an hour, as opposed to waiting days for traditional PCR results to arrive from a lab. This targeted, risk-based testing approach is designed to lower costs and increase effectiveness, so farmers can detect the virus early and reduce its spread. "To stop the spread of HPAI, producers need tools that will enable them to monitor risk and, when it's elevated, employ rapid, accurate tests so they can take quick action and prevent further infection," said Shaun Holt, CEO of Alveo Technologies "This dynamic solution will aggregate and simplify rich data from AgriNerds' and deliver sophisticated risk assessments to users phones in a simple red, yellow and green format. They can then run surveillance tests based on informed risk and rapidly respond if bird flu is detected." The two organizations will use this feedback loop to strengthen the accuracy of risk assessments over time. As positive and negative test data accumulate across regions and seasons, both the risk alerts and testing guidance will become increasingly precise and valuable, securing the nation's food supply as well as producers' businesses. "Biosecurity extends far beyond the facility's fence line," said Maurice Pitesky, professor at UC Davis and CEO and co-founder of AgriNerds. "Our Waterfowl Alert Network gives farmers visibility into the dynamic risk landscape around their operations. When paired with Alveo's testing capability and rapid results, farmers can respond to real risks in real time. In this way, agriculture can move past reactive disease management to adopt a proactive, risk-informed approach." About AgriNerds: AgriNerds' veterinarians, epidemiologists, engineers, and waterfowl biologists are leveraging and repurposing various remote sensing-based technologies and applying modern statistical methods to help farmers usher in practical "off-site" risk assessments and HPAI risk predictions. The WaterFowl Alert Network is used by over 1,500 farms across 25 states and has the capacity to make historic and daily risk predictions for the entire U.S. poultry and livestock industry at the farm level. For more information, visit www.agrinerds.com. About Alveo Technologies: Alveo Technologies is a molecular diagnostics company that has developed a portable, cloud-connected platform that brings laboratory-quality pathogen detection directly to the Point of NeedTM for farmers, veterinarians and public health officials. By decentralizing molecular diagnostics, Alveo enables rapid detection and decision-making to help protect animal and human health, food security and supply chain resiliency. Alveo Sense Poultry provides avian influenza detection in approximately one hour, with results delivered through the Alveo Sense app. The Alveo platform incorporates machine learning technology to analyze assay data and provide automated interpretation of test results. Its growing portfolio includes molecular tests for avian influenza and other high-consequence pathogens. To learn more, visit alveotechnologies.com or follow us on LinkedIn. Product Availability Disclaimer: Product availability may vary by country or jurisdiction and is subject to applicable regulatory requirements and approvals. For information regarding availability in your country or jurisdiction, please contact Alveo Technologies at [email protected]. analysis.event: Australia confirmed the first case of a native mammal infected with H5N1 avian influenza virus, found in a long-nosed fur seal.
analysis.scale_impact_and_risk: The H5N1 virus has been spreading among wild birds in Australia since June, and the infection in the fur seal indicates potential spillover to mammals. The Australian government is monitoring the spread and taking preventive measures.
analysis.response_status_and_uncertainty: The Australian government is investigating the case and has stated that the fur seal's death does not appear to be linked to other marine mammals. The situation is under active monitoring.

analysis.brief_en: Australia has confirmed the first case of a native mammal infected with H5N1 avian influenza virus, found in a long-nosed fur seal in South Australia. The fur seal was discovered dead in the coastal town of Beachport, approximately 310 kilometers south of Adelaide, with no signs of injury. This marks the first known instance of a mammal contracting H5N1 in the country. The Australian government has noted that the infection does not seem to be connected to other marine mammals' deaths. H5N1 was first detected in Australia in June and has since spread among wild birds. Authorities are actively monitoring the situation and have taken preventive measures, including vaccinating wild penguins on Phillip Island to curb the spread of the virus. The case highlights the potential for avian influenza to spill over into mammalian hosts, raising concerns about zoonotic transmission and the need for continued vigilance.

news.content: Australia Rush to vaccinate little penguins against H5N1 as another seal is diagnosed A second seal has contracted the virus in South Australia, as Phillip Island rushes to vaccinate its iconic bird population. Scientists hope to vaccinate the 5,000-strong colony of little penguins on Phillip Island. Source: AAP / Joel Carrett 3 min read Published 24 August 2026 11:22am Source : AAP Skip to article content In brief Five suspected H5 bird flu cases were recorded in South Australia on Monday, including a long-nosed fur seal. 5,000 little penguins in Victoria are receiving a vaccine to protect them against the deadly virus. Bird flu has likely spread to a second seal, one day after the first mammal in Australia was confirmed to have contracted the virus. Five suspected H5 bird flu cases were recorded in South Australia on Monday, including a long-nosed fur seal at The Pages Conservation Park, the state's Department of Primary Industries and Regions said in a statement on Monday morning. The Pages — which covers two small islands between Kangaroo Island and the mainland — is a haven for the endangered Australian sea lion. The fur seal has been tested for bird flu, with results expected in the coming days. The first positive case of the virus in a mammal was confirmed on Sunday in a long-nosed fur seal at Beachport, 300km south of Adelaide, which authorities believed was contracted from wild birds. News that makes sense Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox. Before the new case was announced, Environment Minister Murray Watt said the spread from birds to mammals was inevitable and the government was examining whether further vaccination programs were needed. "We are likely to see mass mortalities of birds and mammals, and I know that is a very distressing thing for Australians to hear. But we also need to be realistic," he told ABC TV on Monday. "This is what we've seen happen overseas. Australia is very fortunate that we've been the last continent on Earth to have this strain of bird flu happen. But we are likely to see those kind of events as we have overseas." Agriculture Minister Julie Collins said the federal government was investigating whether bird flu vaccines were available for use in mammals. "There are trials underway in North America, in California and Hawaii, and this is using a vaccine that's been developed for cattle," she told ABC radio. "There certainly is nothing commercially available, but we do continue to look at that research." Bird flu vaccinations have been rolled out to at-risk species, including the little penguins on Victoria's Phillip Island. Many were corralled into pens to receive the first of two vaccinations on Sunday night. With case numbers on the rise, authorities have stepped in to do what they can to defend the 5,000-strong colony. The penguins' nightly ritual of returning to the same burrow, along the same path, made them ideal candidates for vaccination, Phillip Island Nature Parks reserve manager Ben Thomas said. As a world-first in scale, the process has taken some experimentation and fine-tuning. "We've had our teams out late into the night for a week now and learning a lot along the process," Thomas said. "We started on some of the quieter penguin pathways to fine-tune the whole process and get it working as quickly as we can, so we can process as many penguins as we can each night. "We've now moved to the western end of the penguin parade, where the larger numbers are, and it's working really well." A further 600 penguins were vaccinated over the weekend, taking the total number that have received a first dose at Phillip Island and St Kilda to about 1,000. 全球最后"净土"告破!西澳首现H5N1高致病性禽流感,赫德岛已致逾1.3万头海豹幼崽惨死 新西兰新闻 华人号 2026-06-20 13:06 阅读量:6.6万+ 华人号:新西兰新闻 (本报综合报道)​ 当地时间2026年6月20日,澳大利亚联邦农业、渔业和林业部长朱莉·柯林斯(Julie Collins)正式确认:西澳大利亚州埃斯佩兰斯(Esperance)附近Cape Le Grand国家公园发现的一只野生棕贼鸥(brown skua),经CSIRO检测确诊感染H5N1型高致病性禽流感病毒,同一区域另一只巨鹱鸟初筛亦呈阳性。这意味着,澳大利亚——这个曾被视为全球唯一未受H5型禽流感侵扰的大陆,正式"失守"。 候鸟携毒登陆,西澳偏远海岸现死鸟 据西澳农业部披露,6月14日,珀斯东南约700公里的埃斯佩兰斯以东56公里处海滩,志愿者发现一只行为异常、无法飞行的迁徙海鸟(棕贼鸥),该鸟于当晚死亡,样本连夜送检。6月20日上午,澳大利亚疾病预防中心出具最终报告:确认为H5N1高致病性禽流感阳性,与先前在澳海外领地赫德岛(Heard Island)检出的毒株同源。 联邦首席兽医官贝丝·库克森(Beth Cookson)表示,目前未在家禽养殖场发现感染,也未监测到本土野生动物大规模死亡,但全澳已启动最高级别野生鸟类监测网络,重点盯防黑天鹅、企鹅等易感物种。 南极前哨已沦陷:赫德岛生态惨剧 比本土首例更触目惊心的是,就在病例公布前一天(6月19日),澳大利亚南极项目(AAP)发布权威研究声明:高致病性H5N1禽流感已肆虐澳属亚南极领地——赫德岛及麦克唐纳岛。 无人机航测数据显示: 南象海豹幼崽平均死亡率达76%,部分聚居地高达97%,预估死亡数超13,000头; 王企鹅、巴布亚企鹅及南极毛皮海狮均检出病毒阳性,出现异常死亡; 基因溯源显示病毒可能于2025年8月自法属克罗泽特群岛经野生动物迁徙东传约1800公里抵岛。 生态学家警告,若病毒借候鸟进一步向澳本土湿地、沿海繁殖地扩散,澳洲独有的无尾熊(考拉除外,此处指特有水禽)及海洋哺乳动物将面临"最可怕的噩梦"。 家禽业严阵以待,暂未影响供应链 西澳农业部长杰基·贾维斯(Jackie Jarvis)称,发现点距商业家禽养殖区较远,全澳蛋鸡及肉鸡场暂未检出异常。政府已要求养殖户强化生物安全——必要时下达"圈养令"禁止散养、封堵野鸟接触饮水饲料,防止重演去年H7疫情导致200余万只蛋鸡被扑杀、超市鸡蛋断供的困局。 普通人要恐慌吗?专家:无需,但需警惕 澳洲卫生及公共卫生专家强调:目前无证据表明该毒株具备持续人际传播能力,普通人群感染风险低。人类感染多发生于密切接触染病/死亡动物的情况。 昆士兰大学传染病专家保罗·格里芬(Paul Griffin)教授提醒民众做到三点: 不触碰:发现生病、受伤或死亡的野鸟、海豹等野生动物,严禁徒手接触,保持距离拍照记录位置; 速上报:立即通过各州动物疫病热线(如澳洲1800 675 888)或birdflu.gov.au网站报告; 勤洗手+打疫苗:接触自然环境后认真洗手,季节性流感疫苗按时接种以保护基础免疫力。 澳总理阿尔巴尼斯表示,联邦已投入逾1.13亿澳元建立H5禽流感应对体系,"我们一直为此刻做准备,关键在于科学应对而非盲目焦虑"。 (本报将持续追踪CSIRO对第二只巨鹱鸟的最终分型结果及野生种群监测动态。) 澳联社及《自然》子刊预印本研究报道|2026年6月20日 家禽业严阵以待,暂未影响供应链 西澳农业部长杰基·贾维斯(Jackie Jarvis)称,发现点距商业家禽养殖区较远,全澳蛋鸡及肉鸡场暂未检出异常。政府已要求养殖户强化生物安全——必要时下达"圈养令"禁止散养、封堵野鸟接触饮水饲料,防止重演去年H7疫情导致200余万只蛋鸡被扑杀、超市鸡蛋断供的困局。 普通人要恐慌吗?专家:无需,但需警惕 澳洲卫生及公共卫生专家强调:目前无证据表明该毒株具备持续人际传播能力,普通人群感染风险低。人类感染多发生于密切接触染病/死亡动物的情况。 昆士兰大学传染病专家保罗·格里芬(Paul Griffin)教授提醒民众做到三点: 不触碰:发现生病、受伤或死亡的野鸟、海豹等野生动物,严禁徒手接触,保持距离拍照记录位置; 速上报:立即通过各州动物疫病热线(如澳洲1800 675 888)或birdflu.gov.au网站报告; 勤洗手+打疫苗:接触自然环境后认真洗手,季节性流感疫苗按时接种以保护基础免疫力。 澳总理阿尔巴尼斯表示,联邦已投入逾1.13亿澳元建立H5禽流感应对体系,"我们一直为此刻做准备,关键在于科学应对而非盲目焦虑"。 (本报将持续追踪CSIRO对第二只巨鹱鸟的最终分型结果及野生种群监测动态。) 澳联社及《自然》子刊预印本研究报道|2026年6月20日 analysis.brief_en: The news report highlights the first confirmed case of H5N1 highly pathogenic avian influenza in Western Australia, detected in a wild brown skua near Cape Le Grand National Park. This marks the end of Australia's status as the last continent free from H5-type avian influenza. The virus, which is genetically linked to strains found on Heard Island and McDonald Island, has caused a devastating ecological impact, with over 13,000 seal pups dying on Heard Island, where mortality rates reached 76%-97% in some areas. The outbreak was traced back to a potential transmission from the French Crozet Islands in August 2025 via migratory birds. While no infections have been found in domestic poultry farms, the Australian government has activated a high-level monitoring system for susceptible bird species. Experts emphasize that the risk to the general public remains low, as there is no evidence of sustained human-to-human transmission. However, they advise caution, especially for those in contact with wildlife, and recommend reporting any sick or dead animals and maintaining hygiene. The government has allocated over 1.13 billion Australian dollars to address the outbreak, focusing on scientific response rather than panic.

source_language_evidence.event: 西澳首次发现H5N1高致病性禽流感病毒感染野生棕贼鸥, 赫德岛出现大规模海豹幼崽死亡事件, 病毒通过候鸟迁徙传播至南极亚南极领地。
source_language_evidence.scale_impact_and_risk: 赫德岛海豹幼崽死亡率高达76%-97%, 预计死亡数超13,000头; 巨鹱鸟初筛呈阳性; 病毒可能于2025年8月从法属克罗泽特群岛经迁徙传播至赫德岛; 未在家禽养殖场发现感染, 但已启动最高级别野生鸟类监测网络。
source_language_evidence.response_status_and_uncertainty: 澳大利亚联邦农业、渔业和林业部长朱莉·柯林斯确认感染, 联邦首席兽医官贝丝·库克森启动最高级别监测网络; 澳总理阿尔巴尼斯投入1.13亿澳元建立应对体系; 专家建议公众无需恐慌但需警惕, 并采取防护措施。

analysis.event: Australia's disease control center assessed the risk of human infection with H5N1 as low, with no recorded human cases of H5N1 infection.
analysis.scale_impact_and_risk: Since the H5N1 2.3.4.4b strain emerged in Europe six years ago, there have been 141 global human infections and 24 deaths. analysis.brief_en: Australia's disease control center has assessed the risk of human infection with H5N1 as low, with no recorded cases of human H5N1 infection. The center stated that while the virus has been detected in seals, human-to-human transmission is extremely rare. Globally, since the H5N1 2.3.4.4b strain emerged in Europe six years ago, there have been 141 human infections and 24 deaths, primarily linked to close contact with infected animals. Most cases occur in poultry farm and dairy workers. The virus can spread through direct contact with infected birds, their feces, respiratory secretions, or contaminated dust. Symptoms, which may appear one to ten days after infection, include fever, cough, sore throat, runny nose, muscle pain, headache, fatigue, nausea, and vomiting. The center advises avoiding contact with sick or dead birds, washing hands after handling birds, and thoroughly cooking meat and eggs to reduce risk. The report is a partial syndicated summary, and the full original article could not be accessed.

analysis.event: Australia confirmed its first mammal infection with H5N1 avian influenza in a long-nosed fur seal found dead near Beachport, South Australia. The detection was reported by South Australian authorities on 23 August 2026.
analysis.scale_impact_and_risk: Single confirmed case in a wild long-nosed fur seal; no reported human, poultry, or agricultural infections in Australia. The virus has previously caused large-scale wild bird deaths in Australia since June 2026, with 297 confirmed cases nationwide as of 21 August 2026. Federal officials warn that widespread environmental circulation of H5 avian influenza could lead to significant losses.
analysis.response_status_and_uncertainty: South Australian authorities confirmed the case on 23 August 2026; federal Agriculture Minister stated the death appears unrelated to other sick or dead marine mammals. National testing and surveillance continue; no evidence of H5N1 in Australian poultry or agriculture reported. Investigation ongoing; uncertainty remains regarding transmission pathways to mammals and potential broader ecological impact.

analysis.brief_en: Australia has confirmed its first mammal infection with H5N1 avian influenza after a long-nosed fur seal was found dead near Beachport in South Australia. The case was announced by state authorities on 23 August 2026. The federal agriculture minister warned that widespread circulation of H5 avian influenza in the environment could cause significant losses, though the detected strain has not yet been found in poultry or agricultural settings. The seal showed no visible injuries and its death appears unrelated to other marine mammal mortalities. Australia has been battling a surge in H5N1 cases among wild birds since June, with 297 confirmed cases nationwide as of 21 August. Authorities continue monitoring and testing while investigating potential transmission routes to mammals.

news.content_zh: 在南澳大利亚海滩港附近发现一只长鼻海豹死亡后,澳大利亚确认了首例 H5N1 禽流感 哺乳动物感染。州当局于 2026 年 8 月 23 日宣布了此案。联邦农业部长警告说,尽管尚未在家禽或农业环境中发现检测到的菌株,但 H5 禽流感 在环境中的广泛传播可能会造成重大损失。这只海豹没有明显的受伤迹象,它的死亡似乎与其他海洋哺乳动物的死亡无关。自 6 月以来,澳大利亚一直在应对 野生鸟类 中 H5N1 病例激增的情况,截至 8 月 21 日,全国确诊病例为 297 例。当局继续监测和测试,同时调查 传播 通往哺乳动物的潜在途径。

analysis.event: Australia confirmed the first case of H5N1 avian influenza virus detected in a mammal. The infected long-nosed fur seal was found dead with no signs of injury.
analysis.scale_impact_and_risk: This is the first confirmed case of H5N1 in a mammal in Australia. The virus has been spreading among wild birds, with 297 confirmed cases nationwide. The risk to humans is considered low, as the virus has not been detected in poultry or agricultural sectors.
analysis.response_status_and_uncertainty: The Australian government is monitoring the situation and has stated that the H5N1 virus is not currently present in domestic poultry. The cause of the seal's infection is suspected to be contact with infected wild birds or their environment.

analysis.brief_en: Australia has confirmed the first case of H5N1 avian influenza virus detected in a mammal, specifically a long-nosed fur seal found dead in a coastal town south of Adelaide. The seal showed no signs of injury, and the infection is suspected to have occurred through contact with infected wild birds or their environment. This marks a significant development in the ongoing spread of H5N1 among wild birds, with 297 confirmed cases nationwide. The Australian government has stated that the virus has not been detected in poultry or agricultural sectors, and the risk to humans remains low. This marks a significant development in the ongoing spread of H5N1 among wild birds, with 297 confirmed cases nationwide. The Australian government has stated that the virus has not been detected in poultry or agricultural sectors, and the risk to humans remains low. news.content_title: 澳洲首例哺乳动物患禽流感 海豹遗体检测出H5N1病毒
news.content: 金融 财经 政治 法律 首都动态 国外新闻 教育与文化 华社 科学与技术 社论 评论 健康知识 体育 社会 特别 娱乐 人民福利 宗教 东盟动态 广告 视频 Select Language​▼ 4:16:14 30 °C 雅加达 熱點新聞 【金融】 IHSG周五小幅高开至6,535点 【金融】 盾币周五早盘升至17718盾 【财经】 今日Antam金价小幅下跌 1克价格271万8000盾 【财经】 预计2026下半年印尼煤炭出口稳健 价格在每吨100美元以上 【财经】 工作计划和企业预算削减 开始抑制重型设备销售 2026年 08月 23日 22:25 PM 688 澳洲首例哺乳动物患禽流感 海豹遗体检测出H5N1病毒 - 澳洲首只长鼻毛皮海豹感染禽流感病亡。(示意图) 澳洲首次出现哺乳动物因感染H5N1禽流感病毒而死亡的病例。H5N1是一种特定的、高度传染性的禽流感病毒株,俗称禽流感。 染疫的是一只长鼻毛皮海豹,它于8月19日在南澳州首府阿德莱德以南约310公里石灰岩海岸小镇比奇波特(Beachport)被发现时,已经死亡,身上没有受伤迹象。 澳洲农业部长柯林斯(Julie Collins)在电视讲话中说,这只海豹的死亡似乎同其他患病或死亡的海洋哺乳动物无关,它很可能是因为接触染疫野生鸟类或在同这些鸟类共处的环境中受到感染。 澳洲今年6月首次发现H5型禽流感病毒后,当地感染病例持续增加。南澳州州长马利瑙斯卡斯(Peter Malinauskas)数天前才表示离岸岛屿发生了3起涉及1000多只大凤头燕鸥(greater crested terns)的大规模死亡事件,这标志着病毒传播的进一步升级。 此外,南澳州政府也证实,本周稍早在袋鼠岛( Kangaroo Island)发现的一只小企鹅的H5禽流感病毒检测呈阳性。 南澳州将与联邦政府合作,评估一种来自美国的实验性疫苗是否可以用于澳洲的哺乳动物。 柯林斯表示,人们无法阻止病毒的传播,尤其是在野生鸟类中;如果野生鸟类的死亡数量增加,预计海洋哺乳动物的病例报告也会增加,并表示全国境内共发生了298起事件,其中南澳州183起、维多利亚州86起、新南威尔士州11起、西澳州10起、塔斯马尼亚州7起、昆士兰州1起。 澳洲联邦政府评估认为,长鼻海豹和濒危的澳洲海狮等哺乳动物面临着极高的病毒感染风险,强调H5型禽流感病毒尚未在当地家禽或农业领域出现。 人际传播的风险仍然很低,但当局敦促民众避开生病或死亡的鸟类,并向 birdflu.gov.au网站报告。 澳洲海洋保护协会敦促联邦政府设立2亿澳元的野生动物恢复基金,用于保护面临大规模死亡或局部灭绝风险的濒危物种。 热文推荐 最多阅读者 01IHSG周五小幅高开至6,535点 02盾币周五早盘升至17718盾 03今日Antam金价小幅下跌 1克价格271万8000盾 04印尼塞梅鲁火山六小时内发生21次喷发地震 05刚果(金)埃博拉疫情迅速蔓延 联合国秘书长吁提供援助 01朱一龙领衔主演犯罪电影《空枪》上映第三天 累计票房破亿 02宁德时代参与建设的印尼电芯工厂建成并分阶段投产 年产能6.9吉瓦时 03印尼禁毒局 : 2.6吨液体冰毒走私案告破 04IHSG升至6525点 跟随亚洲股市走强 05QRIS用户达6577万 助力中小微企业“数字升级” 财经 今日Antam金价小幅下跌 1克价格271万8000盾 2026年 08月 28日 09:26 AM 【本报讯】周五(8月28日),Antam金条价格小幅下跌。Antam金条1克价格271万8000盾。 根据... 预计2026下半年印尼煤炭出口稳健 价格在每吨100美元以上 工作计划和企业预算削减 开始抑制重型设备销售 IEU-CEPA 为出口开辟机遇 但企业仍受非关税壁垒困扰 印尼棕榈油产量2027年或减少500万吨 棕榈油出口面临承压风险 查看更多 » 金融 IHSG周五小幅高开至6,535点 2026年 08月 28日 10:25 AM 【本报讯】印尼证券交易所(BEI)综合股价指数(IHSG)周五(28/8)早盘上涨13.97点,涨幅0.21... 盾币周五早盘升至17718盾 国会批准Destry任印尼央行行长 Aida任高级副行长 印尼央行:QRIS手续费不得转嫁给消费者 加密资产用户突破2290万 OJK:截至7月交易额达20.52万亿盾 查看更多 » Original text Rate this translation Your feedback will be used to help improve Google Translate

analysis.time: Published 2026-08-23; event occurred 2026-08-19.
analysis.location_and_population: Australia, South Australia, Beachport (Limestone Coast), and Kangaroo Island; marine mammals (long-nosed fur seal), seabirds (greater crested terns), and penguins.
analysis.event: First confirmed mammalian fatality from H5N1 avian influenza in Australia; reported by Australian Agriculture Minister Julie Collins and South Australia Premier Peter Malinauskas; event is confirmed.
analysis.scale_impact_and_risk: 1 confirmed mammalian death (long-nosed fur seal); 298 total H5 avian influenza events nationwide (183 in South Australia, 86 in Victoria, 11 in New South Wales, 10 in Western Australia, 7 in Tasmania, 1 in Queensland); 1,000+ greater crested tern deaths in offshore islands; 1 penguin tested positive; high risk to endangered Australian sea lions and long-nosed fur seals; human-to-human transmission risk remains low.

analysis.brief_en: Australia confirmed its first mammalian death from H5N1 avian influenza after a long-nosed fur seal carcass tested positive in South Australia’s Beachport on 19 August 2026. The federal agriculture minister stated the infection likely resulted from contact with infected wild birds. Nationwide, 298 H5 events have been recorded, including mass deaths of more than 1,000 greater crested terns and a single positive penguin on Kangaroo Island. Authorities warn that endangered Australian sea lions and fur seals face high infection risk, while human-to-human spread remains low. Federal and state officials are evaluating an experimental US vaccine for mammals and urge the public to report sick or dead birds, as the virus has not yet been detected in domestic poultry.

news.content: Open sidebar 正體 简体 正體 登入 首页即时中国美国国际评论台湾香港健康视频听纪元财经科技娱乐文化生活神韵 各地分网 纽约 旧金山 洛杉矶 波士顿 多伦多 温哥华 台湾 香港 澳洲 欧洲 日本 华府 费城 新泽西 美西北 美南 美中 圣地亚哥 加国亚省 蒙特利尔 新西兰 韩国 首页即时中国美国国际评论台湾香港健康视频听纪元财经科技娱乐文化生活神韵 首页 新闻 国际要闻文章正文 澳洲确认首例哺乳动物感染H5N1禽流感 资料照,图为卫生部门的人员将居民院子里的感染禽流感的鹅带走,准备宰杀焚烧。(Daniel Mihailescu/AFP/GettyImages) 2026-08-2320:13 中港台时间|08-2406:49 更新 人气 270 設為Google新聞首選來源 【大纪元2026年08月23日讯】(大纪元记者王兰报导)澳洲联邦与南澳当局周日(8月23日)证实,该国首次在哺乳动物身上发现高致病性H5N1禽流感病毒。 据路透社报导,在南澳洲沿海小镇比奇波特(Beachport),一只长鼻毛皮海豹(Long-nosed Fur Seal)经检测后证实感染H5N1病毒。 这也是澳洲自高致病性禽流感疫情爆发以来,首次确认病毒由野生鸟类扩散至本土哺乳动物。 南澳洲政府表示,这只毛皮海豹被发现时已经死亡,身上没有明显外伤。比奇波特位于南澳洲首府阿德莱德(Adelaide)以南约310公里。当局估计,南澳洲沿岸水域约有10万只长鼻毛皮海豹。 澳洲联邦农业、渔业与林业部部长朱莉‧柯林斯(Julie Collins)表示,目前没有证据显示这只海豹的死亡与其它患病或死亡的海洋哺乳动物有关。 她说:“一旦H5禽流感在自然环境中传播开来,就无法避免重大损失。” 澳洲近期高致病性禽流感疫情持续扩大,病例不断增加。本月,当地首次出现大规模海鸟死亡事件,显示疫情正在进一步扩大。病毒最初在迁徙海鸟身上被发现,随后开始传播至澳洲本土鸟类。 南澳洲首席兽医官弗鲁恩(Skye Fruean)指出,海豹感染H5N1的风险较高,原因是它们经常栖息在沿海岩石地带,与野生鸟类活动区域非常接近,因此可能长期暴露在高浓度病毒环境中。 澳洲是较晚出现H5N1疫情的地区之一。该病毒直到2025年底才首次在澳洲的亚南极领地赫德岛(Heard Island)被发现。据当地媒体报导,岛上已有超过1.3万只幼年海豹因感染病毒死亡。 澳洲联邦政府表示,目前H5N1病毒尚未在家禽养殖场或农业系统中被发现。截至8月21日,全国累计已确认297宗高致病性禽流感病例。 责任编辑:李天琦# 标签 禽流感哺乳动物澳洲 設為Google新聞首選來源 相关文章 全澳首例 海狗感染H5禽流感 新州南海岸H5禽流感疫情扩散 新增7宗病例 禽流感“海啸”逼近 专家吁总理带领全澳应对 禽流感蔓延至著名景点“企鹅归巢” 如果您有新闻线索或资料给大纪元,请进入安全投稿爆料平台。 留言 大纪元保留删除恶意留言的权利,包括低俗、误导或攻击信仰等内容 新闻排行 视频:西藏吉隆突发山洪 致重大人员伤亡 人气 19466 45岁中国女硕士摆水果摊 曾是房地产总监 人气 19411 【独家】中共出入境管制 52类人名单曝光 人气 12956 时隔7年不忍了 王一博起诉《陈情令》5出品方 人气 12281 香蕉总是很快变黑?买回家先做1件事 人气 8493 奥运冠军刘翔网上求助 上海体育局回应 人气 7716 热门排行榜 视频:西藏吉隆突发山洪 致重大人员伤亡 人气 19466 45岁中国女硕士摆水果摊 曾是房地产总监 人气 19411 【独家】中共出入境管制 52类人名单曝光 人气 12956 时隔7年不忍了 王一博起诉《陈情令》5出品方 人气 12281 香蕉总是很快变黑?买回家先做1件事 人气 8493 奥运冠军刘翔网上求助 上海体育局回应 人气 7716 如果您有新闻线索或资料给我们 请进入安全爆料平台 纪元推荐 阅读更多 两任军委科技委主任落马 知情人曝腐败黑链 人气 3922 深圳30年港资老厂结业 中国制造业寒意加深 人气 4712 河南三地河坝决堤 洪水肆虐 村民损失惨重 人气 3437 广东客携港书被查 深圳海关审查内幕曝光 人气 4500 纪元图解 阅读更多 【图解】美国国旗星条旗的光辉历史 人气 3 【图解】七二零27周年 多国政要吁追究中共罪责 人气 2 【图解】《宪法》——解读美国的根本大法 人气 2 守护善良正义,值得奋战到底 支持我们

analysis.location_and_population: Australia, South Australia, Beachport, approximately 310 km south of Adelaide, with an estimated 100,000 long-nosed fur seals in the coastal waters.
analysis.event: Australia confirmed its first case of a mammal infected with H5N1 avian influenza. The infection was detected in a long-nosed fur seal found dead in Beachport, South Australia.
analysis.scale_impact_and_risk: The H5N1 virus has been spreading from wild birds to native birds in Australia. There are currently 297 confirmed cases of highly pathogenic avian influenza nationwide. The risk of H5N1 infection in seals is high due to their proximity to wild birds.
analysis.response_status_and_uncertainty: The Australian government has confirmed the case and is monitoring the spread of the virus. There is no evidence linking the seal's death to other marine mammals. The virus has not been found in poultry farms or agricultural systems.

analysis.brief_en: Australia confirmed its first case of a mammal infected with H5N1 avian influenza, with a long-nosed fur seal found dead in Beachport, South Australia. The virus, which has been spreading from wild birds to native birds, has not yet been detected in poultry farms or agricultural systems. The Australian government is monitoring the situation, noting that the seal's death is not linked to other marine mammals. The risk of H5N1 infection in seals is high due to their proximity to wild birds. As of August 21, 2026, there have been 297 confirmed cases of highly pathogenic avian influenza nationwide. This marks the first time the virus has been confirmed to spread to native mammals in Australia.

news.content_original: ua en pl ru cn 邮件: 登录 注册 世界 乌克兰 俄乌战争 调查 开放性问题 挺过来的城市 基辅 政治 商业 博彩业 农业 能源 IT与电信 制药 物流与运输 冶金 分析 房地产 技术 体育 电竞 关于生活 健康 文化 美丽 明星 汽车世界 旅行 +13° Kyiv +14° Warsaw +23° Washington $ 44.63 € 52 zł 11.99 世界 乌克兰 俄乌战争 调查 开放性问题 挺过来的城市 基辅 政治 商业 博彩业 农业 能源 IT与电信 制药 物流与运输 冶金 分析 房地产 技术 体育 电竞 关于生活 健康 文化 美丽 明星 汽车世界 旅行 更多... 邮件 登录 注册 cn ua en pl ru cn $ 44.63 € 52 zł 11.99 +13° Kyiv +14° Warsaw +23° Washington 重点 世界 澳大利亚约千只小企鹅接种首剂H5N1疫苗 Лев Шевцов 24 八月 2026 00:03 澳大利亚维多利亚州菲利普岛约有1000只小企鹅接种了首剂H5N1禽流感疫苗。当局计划在菲利普岛和圣基尔达为5000只鸟类接种疫苗,澳大利亚广播公司新闻报道。 两剂接种计划 在过去一周中,工作人员每天傍晚都捕捉并为数百只企鹅接种疫苗。这项两剂接种计划需要约1万剂疫苗。 参加菲利普岛每晚“企鹅巡游”的企鹅计划在三至四周后再次被捕捉,以接种第二剂。维多利亚州环境部长杰克琳·赛姆斯表示,该疫苗应能提高鸟类体内的抗体水平,但目前尚不清楚它是否能防止感染流感。她表示,接种疫苗可能提供一定程度的保护,并帮助企鹅在感染后康复。 更多最新消息请关注 UA.News Telegram 频道 Telegram. 该物种最大的群落 菲利普岛生活着约4万只小企鹅,这是世界上最大的该物种群落。最坏情景模型显示,大规模禽流感暴发可能导致8000至1.6万只鸟类死亡。 菲利普岛自然公园负责人本·托马斯说,企鹅从海滩返回后会被引导进入围栏,随后被转移到较小的围栏中接种疫苗。他指出,团队正努力迅速而谨慎地行动,因为鸟类居住密集,病毒可能迅速在群落中传播。 在第1000只企鹅接种疫苗当天,H5N1毒株在南澳大利亚一只长鼻海狗身上被发现。这是该毒株首次被确认进入澳大利亚哺乳动物种群。菲利普岛自然公园首席执行官凯瑟琳·巴斯特菲尔德认为,如此规模的大规模接种计划可能是世界首例。 关注我们在 Telegram 和 Sends 下载我们的应用程序 ×

analysis.time: Published 2026-08-23; event reported as occurring over the past week with second-dose recapture planned in 3–4 weeks.
analysis.location_and_population: Victoria State, Phillip Island and St Kilda, Australia; wild little penguin (Eudyptula minor) population.
analysis.event: Australian authorities and Phillip Island Nature Parks launched a two-dose H5N1 avian influenza vaccination campaign for wild little penguins; status is reported and ongoing.
analysis.scale_impact_and_risk: Approximately 1,000 penguins received the first dose; total target is 5,000 birds across Phillip Island and St Kilda using about 10,000 vaccine doses. Phillip Island hosts ~40,000 little penguins; worst-case H5N1 outbreak modelling suggests 8,000–16,000 deaths. H5N1 was detected in a South Australian long-nosed fur seal, marking the first confirmed spillover into an Australian mammal population.
analysis.response_status_and_uncertainty: Daily evening captures and vaccinations conducted; second dose recapture planned in 3–4 weeks. Authorities state vaccine aims to raise antibodies but efficacy against infection is unknown; vaccination may provide some protection and aid recovery. Teams act rapidly while minimizing stress due to dense rookeries and risk of rapid viral spread. Further updates are available via UA.News channels.

analysis.brief_en: Australian wildlife authorities and Phillip Island Nature Parks have initiated a two-dose H5N1 avian influenza vaccination campaign for wild little penguins, with about 1,000 birds receiving the first dose over the past week. The effort targets 5,000 penguins across Phillip Island and St Kilda using roughly 10,000 vaccine doses. Phillip Island hosts the world’s largest little penguin colony of around 40,000 birds; modelling warns that a large H5N1 outbreak could kill 8,000–16,000 individuals. The program follows the first detection of H5N1 in an Australian mammal—a long-nosed fur seal in South Australia—raising concerns about spillover risk. Teams are vaccinating penguins nightly while minimizing stress, and a second dose is planned in 3–4 weeks; authorities note the vaccine may raise antibodies but its ability to prevent infection remains unproven.

news.content_zh: 澳大利亚野生动物管理局和菲利普岛自然公园已针对野生小企鹅发起了两剂 H5N1 禽流感 疫苗接种 活动,过去一周已有约 1,000 只鸟类接受了第一剂疫苗。这项工作的目标是菲利普岛和圣基尔达的 5,000 只企鹅,使用了大约 10,000 剂 疫苗 剂量。菲利普岛 宿主 是世界上最大的小企鹅栖息地,拥有约 40,000 只鸟类;模型警告称,大型 H5N1 暴发 可能会导致 8,000-16,000 人死亡。该计划是在澳大利亚哺乳动物(南澳大利亚的长鼻海狗)中首次检测到 H5N1 病毒之后进行的,引发了人们对 跨物种溢出 风险的担忧。团队每晚为企鹅接种疫苗,同时最大程度地减少压力,并计划在 3-4 周内注射第二剂疫苗;当局指出,疫苗 可能会产生抗体,但其预防感染的能力尚未得到证实。

× 澳大利亚确认首例哺乳动物感染H5N1禽流感病例 By 新西兰中文先驱网· 2026年08月24日 10:54 禽流感 分享 听新闻▶0:00/0:00✕ 顶部 侨报讯 澳大利亚周日确认首例哺乳动物感染H5N1禽流感病例,在南澳大利亚州一只长吻毛皮海豹体内检测到这种致命病毒。 据路透社报道,澳大利亚自6月首次出现H5N1禽流感后,疫情持续扩大。本月,该国首次出现大规模海鸟死亡事件,标志着疫情进一步升级。病毒最初在迁徙海鸟中被发现,随后扩散至当地野生动物。 南澳大利亚州有关部门确认,在距离州首府阿德莱德约310公里的海滨小镇比奇波特(Beachport)发现了这只死亡海豹。这只海豹没有明显外伤。当地水域估计约有10万只同类海豹。 澳大利亚联邦农业部长朱莉·柯林斯(Julie Collins)在电视讲话中表示,这只海豹的死亡“似乎与其他患病或死亡的海洋哺乳动物没有关联”。她说,一旦H5N1禽流感开始在自然环境中传播,“就不可能避免出现重大损失”。 澳大利亚是全球最后一个报告禽流感疫情的大陆。不过,2025年年底,病毒已经在澳大利亚的亚南极领地赫德岛(Heard Island)被发现。据当地媒体报道,病毒已导致岛上超过1.3万只幼年海豹死亡。 南澳大利亚州首席兽医官斯凯·弗鲁恩(Skye Fruean)表示,海豹感染H5N1的风险较高,因为它们经常生活在海岸岩礁附近,与野生鸟类距离很近。 她说,这些海豹“毫无疑问会在环境中接触到非常高水平的病毒”。 不过,澳大利亚联邦政府表示,目前尚未在该国的家禽或农业生产体系中发现H5N1。政府周五公布的数据显示,全国目前已确认297例禽流感病例。 随着H5N1从野生鸟类向哺乳动物扩散,澳大利亚当局正密切关注病毒是否进一步传播至更多海洋哺乳动物。 相关阅读: 新西兰发现第三例H5禽流感病例 新州致命禽流感疫情持续扩散,本土鸟类首次确诊!全澳确诊总数升至215例 H5禽流感在澳扩散,海滩现大量死鸟,专家忧心“进入下一阶段” 为防禽流感,55万只散养鸡进入封闭管理,超市呼吁勿抢购囤积 新西兰确认第二例H5N1禽流感!本土鸟类中招,家禽业高度戒备! 禽流感病例首现,专家警告这类物种面临巨大风险!环保部正在行动! 新西兰确诊首例H5禽流感病例!鸡蛋要涨价了? × 澳大利亚确认首例哺乳动物感染H5N1禽流感病例 By 新西兰中文先驱网· 2026年08月24日 10:54 禽流感 分享 听新闻▶0:00/0:00✕ 顶部 侨报讯 澳大利亚周日确认首例哺乳动物感染H5N1禽流感病例,在南澳大利亚州一只长吻毛皮海豹体内检测到这种致命病毒。 据路透社报道,澳大利亚自6月首次出现H5N1禽流感后,疫情持续扩大。本月,该国首次出现大规模海鸟死亡事件,标志着疫情进一步升级。病毒最初在迁徙海鸟中被发现,随后扩散至当地野生动物。 南澳大利亚州有关部门确认,在距离州首府阿德莱德约310公里的海滨小镇比奇波特(Beachport)发现了这只死亡海豹。这只海豹没有明显外伤。当地水域估计约有10万只同类海豹。 澳大利亚联邦农业部长朱莉·柯林斯(Julie Collins)在电视讲话中表示,这只海豹的死亡“似乎与其他患病或死亡的海洋哺乳动物没有关联”。她说,一旦H5N1禽流感开始在自然环境中传播,“就不可能避免出现重大损失”。 澳大利亚是全球最后一个报告禽流感疫情的大陆。不过,2025年年底,病毒已经在澳大利亚的亚南极领地赫德岛(Heard Island)被发现。据当地媒体报道,病毒已导致岛上超过1.3万只幼年海豹死亡。 南澳大利亚州首席兽医官斯凯·弗鲁恩(Skye Fruean)表示,海豹感染H5N1的风险较高,因为它们经常生活在海岸岩礁附近,与野生鸟类距离很近。 她说,这些海豹“毫无疑问会在环境中接触到非常高水平的病毒”。 不过,澳大利亚联邦政府表示,目前尚未在该国的家禽或农业生产体系中发现H5N1。政府周五公布的数据显示,全国目前已确认297例禽流感病例。 随着H5N1从野生鸟类向哺乳动物扩散,澳大利亚当局正密切关注病毒是否进一步传播至更多海洋哺乳动物。 相关阅读: 新西兰发现第三例H5禽流感病例 新州致命禽流感疫情持续扩散,本土鸟类首次确诊!全澳确诊总数升至215例 H5禽流感在澳扩散,海滩现大量死鸟,专家忧心“进入下一阶段” 为防禽流感,55万只散养鸡进入封闭管理,超市呼吁勿抢购囤积 新西兰确认第二例H5N1禽流感!本土鸟类中招,家禽业高度戒备! 禽流感病例首现,专家警告这类物种面临巨大风险!环保部正在行动! 新西兰确诊首例H5禽流感病例!鸡蛋要涨价了? analysis.time: Published 2026-08-24 10:54 NZST; event reported as occurring on 2026-08-23 (Sunday).
analysis.location_and_population: Australia, South Australia state, Beachport coastal town (~310 km from Adelaide); marine mammal population (estimated 100,000 long-nosed fur seals).
analysis.event: Australia confirmed its first mammal case of H5N1 avian influenza in a long-nosed fur seal found dead in Beachport. The report is based on official confirmation by South Australian authorities and federal statements.
analysis.scale_impact_and_risk: Single confirmed mammal case (one dead long-nosed fur seal). No human cases reported. H5N1 detected in wild birds in Australia since June 2026, with large-scale seabird die-offs this month. No detection in domestic poultry or agricultural systems as of report date. Risk to marine mammals described as high due to close contact with wild birds.

analysis.location_and_population: Beachport, South Australia, Australia; national scope including South Australia, Victoria, New South Wales, Western Australia, Tasmania, and Queensland.
analysis.event: A long-nosed fur seal found dead in Beachport tested positive for H5N1 avian influenza, marking Australia’s mainland first confirmed mammalian infection. Reported by the South Australian government and cited by the federal Minister for Agriculture.
analysis.scale_impact_and_risk: One confirmed mammalian case (long-nosed fur seal); national cumulative 298 avian influenza cases (South Australia 183, Victoria 86, New South Wales 11, Western Australia 10, Tasmania 7, Queensland 1). Human transmission risk remains low; authorities advise avoiding sick or dead birds and reporting sightings. High risk to marine mammals including endangered Australian sea lions.
analysis.response_status_and_uncertainty: South Australia is collaborating with the federal government to assess a US experimental vaccine for use in Australian mammals. Investigation ongoing; officials acknowledge inability to stop viral spread among wild birds and expect increased marine mammal detections if wild bird mortality rises.

analysis.brief_en: Australia’s mainland has recorded its first confirmed case of H5N1 avian influenza in a mammal after a long-nosed fur seal found dead on 19 August in Beachport, South Australia, tested positive. The federal Agriculture Minister described the finding as distressing yet unsurprising, noting the animal likely acquired the virus through contact with infected wild birds or shared environment. Nationally, 298 avian influenza detections have been reported, with South Australia accounting for the majority. Human-to-human transmission risk is assessed as low, and authorities urge the public to avoid sick or dead birds and report sightings. South Australia is now evaluating a US-developed experimental vaccine for potential use in local mammals as part of the response.

analysis.brief_en: On August 23, 2026, Australian authorities confirmed the first case of H5N1 avian influenza in a mammalian host, a long-nosed fur seal found dead in Beachport, South Australia, without external injuries. This marks the first time the virus has been detected in a mammal in Australia. The outbreak has been ongoing since June, with 297 confirmed cases nationwide, primarily affecting birds. While the risk to humans remains low, officials urge the public to avoid contact with sick or dead birds and report any sightings. The virus has spread from migratory birds to local species, raising concerns about its potential to cause significant losses in natural environments. The incident highlights the growing threat of H5N1 in Australia and the need for continued monitoring and public awareness.

news.content_zh: 2026年8月23日,澳大利亚当局在哺乳动物宿主中确认了首例H5N1 禽流感病例,这是一只在南澳大利亚海滩港发现死亡的长鼻海狗,没有外伤。这标志着首次在澳大利亚的哺乳动物中检测到该病毒。暴发 自 6 月以来一直在持续,全国已有 297 例确诊病例,主要影响鸟类。尽管对人类的风险仍然很低,但官员们敦促公众避免接触患病或死亡的鸟类,并报告任何目击事件。该病毒已从候鸟传播到当地物种,引发人们对其可能对自然环境造成重大损失的担忧。该事件凸显了 H5N1 在澳大利亚日益严重的威胁以及持续监测和提高公众意识的必要性。

news.excerpt: A new study reveals how a wide range of factors impact the sector’s capabilities in preparing for, and responding to, outbreaks of highly pathogenic avian influenza.

news.content: ___ × Market Information Top Poultry Companies Expert Insights Blogs Regions Magazines Sign In Poultry Meat Egg Poultry Health Sustainability Poultry Future Chicken Marketing Summit Poultry Tech Summit Broilers & Turkeys Diseases & Health Avian Influenza Poultry industry structure affects resilience to avian flu A new study reveals how a wide range of factors impact the sector’s capabilities in preparing for, and responding to, outbreaks of highly pathogenic avian influenza. Jackie Linden August 26, 2026 Alena Ozihilevich | Bigstock Article Summary Poultry industry resilience to highly pathogenic avian influenza depends not only on biosecurity practices but also on broader structural factors including farm planning decisions, location determined by local authorities, infrastructure, and access to avian flu insurance. A Royal Veterinary College study found that limited insurance options and planning constraints significantly affect how farms manage and recover from HPAI outbreaks. Planning and location decisions by local authorities significantly impact farm resilience, as they must balance farmer interests with community and environmental considerations Insurance availability is limited, making financial risk management a critical business challenge during outbreaks and recovery Each poultry sub-sector (meat, eggs, and game birds) faces distinct HPAI-related challenges requiring tailored resilience strategies Biosecurity alone is insufficient — industry-wide structural factors play an equally important role in protecting against avian flu Europe recorded 311 HPAI outbreaks in farmed poultry across 16 countries in 2026, with Poland leading at 143 cases Just one new highly pathogenic avian influenza (HPAI) outbreak involving poultry has occurred in Europe since the end of July — further evidence of a seasonal lull in infections during the summer months in the northern hemisphere. However, reports of new infections in wild birds across the continent over this period suggests the H5N1 HPAI virus could return with a vengeance as the autumn/fall approaches. It is widely accepted that the maintenance of high standards of biosecurity help to protect poultry on individual farms from HPAI. However, a recently published study reveals that more general factors in the industry also have a role to play. Among those factors impacting the poultry sector in Great Britain are planning, infrastructure, and financial risk, according to the Royal Veterinary College (RVC). From the RVC’s study in cooperation with the University of Cambridge, planning decisions and insurance emerge as key issues affecting resilience to HPAI. Where a poultry farm is located depends on a decision by the local authority, which aims to balance the interests of the farmer with those of the wider community as well as environmental considerations, the study found. With limited options for avian flu insurance, financial risk is also an important business consideration, particularly as producers consider how they will manage firstly the outbreak, and then the recovery of the business. From the study, the researchers also noted that each poultry industry sub-sector — poultry meat, eggs, and game birds — face slightly different HPAI-related challenges. The RVC’s research paper — entitled “Negotiating security and resilience: planning conundrums for avian influenza control in Great Britain’s poultry systems” by M. Hennessey and others — is published in the journal Environmental Research: Food Systems. In the 2025-2026 HPAI “season” (starting October 1, 2025), there were 100 confirmed outbreaks in the poultry in the United Kingdom (U.K.), according to the government agriculture department, Defra. All involved the H5N1 HPAI virus serotype. Of the total, 79 outbreaks occurred in England, nine in Scotland, seven in Wales, and five in Northern Ireland. No new cases in poultry have been recorded in the U.K. since the start of May. HPAI situation in Europe’s domestic birds Over the past four weeks, just one HPAI outbreak in commercial poultry has been reported in Europe. Affected was a small commercial egg farm in the southwest of Sweden, according to an official notification from the national veterinary agency to the World Organisation for Animal Health (WOAH). Presence of the H5N1 virus variant was confirmed in the flock of 145 birds in the municipality of Tanum in mid-August. This was Sweden’s third outbreak in poultry so far this year, based on the Animal Disease Information System (as of August 19). This database from the European Commission (EC) monitors listed animal diseases in European Union member states and selected adjacent countries (but not Great Britain). So far this year, there have been 311 HPAI outbreaks in farmed poultry across Europe, with one or more outbreaks registered by 16 countries. All outbreaks have involved the H5N1 virus variant. Poland’s total is the highest at 143, followed by Germany (40), France (20), and Italy (19). During the whole of 2025, 729 outbreaks in this category occurred in 23 countries. The EC’s System records HPAI outbreaks involving backyard poultry, ornamental flocks, zoos, and similar premises in a separate category as “captive birds.” With no new cases in the past month, the region’s outbreak total in this population so far in 2026 remains unchanged at 119 in 15 countries. Sporadic new cases in European wild birds Since July 31, a total of 19 new HPAI outbreaks involving the wild bird population have been recorded in five of the region’s states by the EC System. Of these, 13 were confirmed in the Netherlands, while Finland, Germany, Norway, and Sweden account for the remaining cases. These bring the outbreak total in Europe’s wild population for the year to date to 2,672 (as of August 19), with one or more cases reported in 32 countries. The H5N1 serotype was detected in more than 2,630 of these outbreaks. For the other outbreaks, the virus was identified as belonging to the H5 “family.” Not included in the EC’s System are disease developments in Great Britain. Earlier this month, a wild goose found dead in north Wales tested positive for the H5N1 virus variant, according to a recent WOAH notification. analysis.brief_en: A new study reveals that the structure of the poultry industry significantly affects its resilience to highly pathogenic avian influenza (HPAI). The research, conducted by the Royal Veterinary College and the University of Cambridge, highlights that factors such as planning decisions, infrastructure, and financial risk management play a crucial role in how farms respond to HPAI outbreaks. In the 2025-2026 HPAI season, the U.K. recorded 100 confirmed outbreaks, all involving the H5N1 virus variant, with the highest number in England. Europe saw 311 HPAI outbreaks in farmed poultry across 16 countries, with Poland leading at 143 cases. Wild birds in Europe have experienced 2,672 outbreaks so far in 2026, with the H5N1 serotype detected in over 2,630 of these. The study emphasizes that biosecurity alone is insufficient, and industry-wide structural factors are equally important in protecting against avian flu. The HPAI situation in Europe is under ongoing monitoring, with only one new outbreak in commercial poultry reported in the past four weeks. However, the presence of H5N1 in wild birds suggests a potential resurgence as autumn approaches.

news.content: English Login Homepage Topic News Political System Destination Event Travel Happy Vietnam Enterprise Product Heritage Museum Figure Multimedia Data Home University Vietnam Academy of Agriculture Scientific workshop “H9N2 and IBV co-infection in poultry: Epidemiological challenges and comprehensive prevention solutions” To celebrate the 70th anniversary of the establishment of the Faculty of Veterinary Medicine and the Vietnam Academy of Agriculture (October 12, 1956 – October 12, 2026), and to strengthen the connection between training, scientific research, and businesses, on August 21, 2026, the Faculty of Veterinary Medicine, Vietnam Academy of Agriculture, in collaboration with VINODA Company and Kemin Vietnam Company, organized a scientific workshop on the theme “H9N2 and IBV Co-infection in Poultry: Epidemiological Challenges and Comprehensive Prevention Solutions” within the framework of the Kemin Education Series. Việt Nam•24/08/2026 Follow Vietnam.vn on Google Add Vietnam.vn on Google 0 The program took place from 1:30 PM to 5:00 PM in Room 409, Faculty of Veterinary Medicine, with the participation of the Faculty leadership, business representatives, experts, lecturers, and a large number of students from the Faculty of Veterinary Medicine. Updating in-depth knowledge about H9N2 and IBV in poultry. Attending the workshop were, on behalf of the Faculty of Veterinary Medicine, Assoc. Prof. Dr. Bui Tran Anh Dao – Head of the Faculty of Veterinary Medicine and Assoc. Prof. Dr. Nguyen Hoai Nam – Deputy Head of the Faculty of Veterinary Medicine. Representing the business sector were Mr. Pham Van Hien – Kemin representative for the Northern and Central regions of Vietnam and Ms. Le My Khanh Huyen – Director of VINODA, along with experts, speakers, and students from the Faculty of Veterinary Medicine. Scientific Workshop: “H9N2 and IBV Co-infection in Poultry: Epidemiological Challenges and Comprehensive Prevention Solutions” Speaking at the workshop, Assoc. Prof. Dr. Bui Tran Anh Dao – Head of the Faculty of Veterinary Medicine – highly appreciated the companionship and support of businesses for the training and professional development activities of the Faculty. According to Assoc. Prof. Dr. Bui Tran Anh Dao, the workshop is a meaningful activity in the series of programs celebrating the 70th anniversary of the Faculty of Veterinary Medicine and the Vietnam Academy of Agriculture , and also provides an opportunity for lecturers and students to update new information on epidemiology as well as advanced biosafety solutions in controlling poultry diseases. Assoc. Prof. Dr. Bui Tran Anh Dao – Head of the Faculty of Veterinary Medicine, delivered the opening remarks at the workshop. Continuing the program, Mr. Pham Van Hien – representative of Kemin Vietnam – affirmed his desire to continue collaborating with the Academy and the Faculty of Veterinary Medicine in training activities, sharing professional knowledge, and connecting business practices with the university. The Kemin Vietnam representative also highly appreciated the learning environment, the foundation of professional knowledge, and the quality of human resources of graduates from the Faculty of Veterinary Medicine, Vietnam Academy of Agriculture. Mr. Pham Van Hien – representative of Kemin Vietnam, spoke at the seminar. At the workshop, the two speakers provided up-to-date and practical professional content on important infectious diseases in poultry. Dr. Dang Huu Anh presented a topic on "Overview of Avian Influenza Virus H9N2 (AIV) and Infectious Bronchitis Virus (IBV) in Chickens," focusing on providing fundamental and updated knowledge about the epidemiological characteristics, causative agents, and challenges in controlling H9N2 and IBV in poultry farming. Dr. Dang Huu Anh presented a specialized topic at the conference. Next, Dr. Wei Shen presented a topic on solutions for controlling H9N2-IBV co-infection using advanced biological methods, and introduced the solution direction from Kemin Biologics and VINODA. The report provided students with a practical perspective on the relationship between co-infection, disease progression, and prevention and control solutions in current production conditions. Dr. Wei Shen presented a paper at the conference. Lively discussions, strengthening connections between training and businesses. One of the topics that students were most interested in at the workshop was the Q&A session and professional discussion. Questions focused on epidemiological characteristics, the phenomenon of co-infection with H9N2 and IBV, factors affecting disease prevention effectiveness, and appropriate control solutions in poultry farming. The exchange was lively and open among students, lecturers, experts, and business representatives. Through this, students had the opportunity to reinforce their classroom knowledge with issues currently facing production, while simultaneously enhancing their professional thinking skills and their ability to access new trends in the veterinary field. Mr. Pham Van Hien – representative of Kemin Vietnam in the discussion Within the framework of the program, Ms. Le My Khanh Huyen – Director of VINODA – shared her desire to have a long-term partnership with the Faculty of Veterinary Medicine in training and developing human resources. VINODA hopes that more students from the Faculty of Veterinary Medicine will participate in internships, experience the corporate environment, and become high-quality human resources to work with the company in the future. The VINODA representative also affirmed their commitment to continue cooperating with the Faculty in professional activities, training, and sharing practical knowledge. Speakers and delegates participating in the discussion at the conference. The insights shared by businesses not only open up opportunities for collaboration in training but also help students better understand the practical requirements of the labor market, thereby proactively supplementing their knowledge, skills, and career orientation while still in school. Continuing the Kemin Education series of activities – Connecting training with practice. The workshop “H9N2 and IBV Co-infection in Poultry: Epidemiological Challenges and Comprehensive Prevention Solutions” is a practical activity in the Kemin Education Series, contributing to the creation of an academic space and professional exchange between the university, experts, and businesses. Through this series of programs, students of the Faculty of Veterinary Medicine gain access to new knowledge, practical issues in production, and technological solutions being researched and applied by businesses. This is also one of the important directions of the Faculty of Veterinary Medicine in innovating training methods, strengthening learning linked to practice, and expanding connections with businesses. The program concluded with a mini-game with many attractive prizes for participating students, creating a cheerful atmosphere and leaving many positive impressions. Representatives from Vinoda and Kemin Vietnam The workshop provided students of the Faculty of Veterinary Medicine with up-to-date knowledge on the epidemiology of H9N2 and IBV, co-infection phenomena, and solutions for disease prevention and control in the context of poultry farming facing increasing disease challenges. This was not only a valuable academic activity but also a testament to the increasingly close collaboration between the Faculty of Veterinary Medicine – Vietnam Academy of Agriculture and Enterprises and businesses, contributing to building a modern, practical, and integrated training environment; and creating more opportunities for students to learn, experience, and develop their careers in the future. Some photos from the workshop. news.content_zh: 2026 年 8 月 21 日,关于家禽中 H9N2 和 IBV 混合感染的科学研讨会在越南河内越南农业科学院兽医学院举行。该活动是与 VINODA 和越南建明公司合作举办的,旨在应对流行病学挑战,并为家禽养殖中的这些感染提供全面的预防解决方案。Dang Huu Anh和Wei Shen等专家发表了演讲,讨论了H9N2和IBV的特征、它们的混合感染现象以及疾病控制的先进生物方法。研讨会还包括问答环节以及学生、讲师和企业代表之间的热烈讨论,以实践见解强化课堂知识。该活动是建明教育系列的一部分,旨在庆祝兽医学院成立 70 周年并促进学术界与工业界之间的合作。没有报告具体病例数或风险水平,但研讨会强调了生物安全解决方案在管理家禽疾病方面的重要性。Vietnam.vn 于 2026 年 8 月 24 日发布了该新闻报道,强调了该活动的教育和专业价值。

维州调整SRL东线方案 / 专家称食品未来或上涨 / 墨尔本Monash发现H5N1禽流感 2 天前来源: 澳大利亚大华时代503分享到: 7收藏6赞 维州调整SRL东线方案 维州大型基建项目郊区铁路环线(Suburban Rail Loop,SRL)长期因成本上涨和财政压力受到争议。新任州长Ben Carroll上任后决定继续推进项目,但通过削减部分设计内容和调整管理方式,降低建设成本。 Carroll于8月25日宣布,SRL East(东线)将削减约20亿澳元成本。其中约10亿澳元来自取消部分“非必要”设计,另外10亿澳元节省目标将通过独立技术评估寻找。SRL East原预算最高约345亿澳元,调整后目标降至约323亿澳元。 根据调整方案,Box Hill和Glen Waverley车站原计划建设的地下换乘设施将取消,改为地面换乘方式;Clayton车站第二个出入口将取消,Burwood和Cheltenham车站复杂的人行天桥设计也将调整。此外,部分停车设施和社区配套项目也会缩减。 除了工程调整,政府还将重组项目管理架构,撤销独立运作的郊区铁路环线管理局(Suburban Rail Loop Authority),相关职能并入维州基础设施交付机构(Victorian Infrastructure Delivery Authority)。 Carroll表示,已经签署的合同和现有工程不会暂停,但在独立技术评估完成前,政府不会签署新的建设合同。 专家称食品未来或上涨 能源专家表示,伊朗冲突带来的通胀压力目前还没有明显反映在澳洲食品价格中,但随着燃料、肥料等农业成本上升,未来食品价格可能面临上涨压力。 麦考瑞大学高级讲师Lurion De Mello表示,霍尔木兹海峡是全球重要石油和化肥运输通道,冲突已经推高部分生产成本。不过,从农场到超市需要一定时间,影响可能要到未来几个月甚至明年才逐渐体现。 目前澳洲食品价格上涨主要不是由伊朗冲突导致。截至6月的一年内,食品和非酒精饮料价格上涨3.3%,其中羊肉和山羊肉上涨14.9%,牛肉和小牛肉上涨11.9%,主要原因是海外需求增加。 De Mello表示,未来受影响较大的可能是依赖进口的食品,例如部分罐头、豆类和意大利面等,因为运输和生产成本增加。不过,澳洲本身是小麦等农产品出口国,全球粮食价格波动对面包等日常食品的影响相对有限。他也提醒,消费者无需提前大量囤货,真正的价格变化还需要观察未来几个月的数据。 墨尔本Monash发现H5N1禽流感 Monash市议会8月25日表示,当地已经确认出现H5N1禽流感。卫生部门目前认为这种病毒对普通居民构成的风险仍然较低,但市民需要避免直接接触患病或死亡的野生动物。 居民不要触摸野生鸟类、羽毛、粪便或鸟蛋,也应让儿童和宠物远离相关区域。遇到行动异常、无法飞行或已经死亡的野生动物时,不建议自行检查。 维州把同一地点出现五只或以上患病、死亡野鸟视为需要报告的禽流感事件。即使只有一只海鸟、水鸟、滨鸟、猛禽或海洋哺乳动物出现异常,也应拨打1800 675 888报告。 如果动物位于Monash市议会管理的土地上,可致电9518 3555安排处理。必须清理自家土地上的死鸟时,应穿长袖衣物和手套,使用铲子或夹具,将动物双层密封后放入红盖垃圾桶,并彻底清洗双手、衣物和工具。 维州流感和新冠感染开始回升 维州首席卫生官麦克尔内(Caroline McElnay)发布最新健康警报,提醒居民近期流感和新冠感染数量正在增加,而且今年的上升时间晚于往年。 维州卫生厅表示,呼吸道合胞病毒(RSV)病例在7月达到高峰后仍处于较高水平,因呼吸道疾病前往医疗机构就诊的人数也在增加。 幼儿、孕妇、老年人、免疫力较弱者及患有基础疾病的人,出现重症和住院的风险相对较高。卫生部门表示,现在接种流感疫苗仍不算晚,部分居民可以免费接种。 居民出现发烧、咳嗽、喉咙痛或全身疲劳等症状时,应尽量留在家中。维州卫生厅还建议勤洗手、遮掩咳嗽和喷嚏,并可通过家庭医生远程问诊、Nurse-on-Call或维州虚拟急诊寻求帮助。 新州老虎机强制使用人脸识别 Mission负责人Stu Cameron表示,政府仍没有采取足够强有力的行动解决老虎机带来的长期问题。 Ballarat PopCon将于9月回归 据Ballarat市议会8月25日消息,年度流行文化活动PopCon Ballarat将于9月27日举行,地点设在Ballarat Library和Civic Hall,活动时间为上午11时至下午4时。活动免费开放,面向各年龄段的动漫、游戏、电影、科幻和奇幻文化爱好者。 今年活动现场将设置超过50个摊位,并提供角色扮演(Cosplay)、桌游、游戏体验、乐高展示、艺术创作和手工工作坊等内容。主办方希望通过活动,让当地居民展示创意,并与兴趣相同的人交流。 活动亮点之一是今年新增的真人角色扮演体验,由当地团体Imagined Realms提供。此外,Cosplay比赛将在当天下午2时30分举行,没有报名参赛的参与者也可以参加服装巡游,展示自己的角色造型。 PopCon由Ballarat青年组织Sonika和Ballarat市议会青年服务团队共同策划。活动自2017年推出以来逐渐扩大规模,并于2025年转移到更大的Ballarat Library和Civic Hall举办,成为维州西部地区较受欢迎的免费流行文化活动之一。 Carroll于8月25日宣布,SRL East(东线)将削减约20亿澳元成本。其中约10亿澳元来自取消部分“非必要”设计,另外10亿澳元节省目标将通过独立技术评估寻找。SRL East原预算最高约345亿澳元,调整后目标降至约323亿澳元。 根据调整方案,Box Hill和Glen Waverley车站原计划建设的地下换乘设施将取消,改为地面换乘方式;Clayton车站第二个出入口将取消,Burwood和Cheltenham车站复杂的人行天桥设计也将调整。此外,部分停车设施和社区配套项目也会缩减。 除了工程调整,政府还将重组项目管理架构,撤销独立运作的郊区铁路环线管理局(Suburban Rail Loop Authority),相关职能并入维州基础设施交付机构(Victorian Infrastructure Delivery Authority)。 Carroll表示,已经签署的合同和现有工程不会暂停,但在独立技术评估完成前,政府不会签署新的建设合同。 专家称食品未来或上涨
