source_language_evidence.brief_en: 墨尔本 返回旧版首页 下载yeeyi App 商务合作 帮助 新版反馈 发布信息 登录/注册 新闻亿部落分类信息用户 租房招聘二手家具搬家清洁屋顶维护宠物二手教材 本地资讯 房屋租赁 房屋交易 车辆交易 求职招聘 二手市场 生意买卖 宠物交易 会计税务 物流搬运 清洁通渠 园艺绿化 水管电工 保姆月嫂 建筑家装 驾校招生 贷 款 生活服务 首页 澳洲 正文 维州调整SRL东线方案 / 专家称食品未来或上涨 / 墨尔本Monash发现H5N1禽流感 2 天前来源: 澳大利亚大华时代503分享到: 7收藏6赞 维州调整SRL东线方案 维州大型基建项目郊区铁路环线(Suburban Rail Loop,SRL)长期因成本上涨和财政压力受到争议。新任州长Ben Carroll上任后决定继续推进项目,但通过削减部分设计内容和调整管理方式,降低建设成本。 Carroll于8月25日宣布,SRL East(东线)将削减约20亿澳元成本。其中约10亿澳元来自取消部分“非必要”设计,另外10亿澳元节省目标将通过独立技术评估寻找。SRL East原预算最高约345亿澳元,调整后目标降至约323亿澳元。 根据调整方案,Box Hill和Glen Waverley车站原计划建设的地下换乘设施将取消,改为地面换乘方式;Clayton车站第二个出入口将取消,Burwood和Cheltenham车站复杂的人行天桥设计也将调整。此外,部分停车设施和社区配套项目也会缩减。 除了工程调整,政府还将重组项目管理架构,撤销独立运作的郊区铁路环线管理局(Suburban Rail Loop Authority),相关职能并入维州基础设施交付机构(Victorian Infrastructure Delivery Authority)。 Carroll表示,已经签署的合同和现有工程不会暂停,但在独立技术评估完成前,政府不会签署新的建设合同。 专家称食品未来或上涨 能源专家表示,伊朗冲突带来的通胀压力目前还没有明显反映在澳洲食品价格中,但随着燃料、肥料等农业成本上升,未来食品价格可能面临上涨压力。 麦考瑞大学高级讲师Lurion De Mello表示,霍尔木兹海峡是全球重要石油和化肥运输通道,冲突已经推高部分生产成本。不过,从农场到超市需要一定时间,影响可能要到未来几个月甚至明年才逐渐体现。

news.content: ua en pl ru cn 邮件: 登录 注册 世界 乌克兰 俄乌战争 调查 开放性问题 挺过来的城市 基辅 政治 商业 博彩业 农业 能源 IT与电信 制药 物流与运输 冶金 分析 房地产 技术 体育 电竞 关于生活 健康 文化 美丽 明星 汽车世界 旅行 +13° Kyiv +14° Warsaw +23° Washington $ 44.63 € 52 zł 11.99 世界 乌克兰 俄乌战争 调查 开放性问题 挺过来的城市 基辅 政治 商业 博彩业 农业 能源 IT与电信 制药 物流与运输 冶金 分析 房地产 技术 体育 电竞 关于生活 健康 文化 美丽 明星 汽车世界 旅行 更多... 邮件 登录 注册 cn ua en pl ru cn $ 44.63 € 52 zł 11.99 +13° Kyiv +14° Warsaw +23° Washington 重点 世界 澳大利亚野生动物园将为100只鸟接种H5N1疫苗 Лев Шевцов 25 八月 2026 10:57 位于南澳大利亚阿德莱德山区的克莱兰野生动物园计划为约100只圈养本土鸟类接种疫苗,以保护它们免受H5N1禽流感侵害。据澳大利亚广播公司新闻报道,该机构成为南澳大利亚首个获得联邦政府批准为鸟类使用该疫苗的野生动物园。 保护稀有物种 将接种疫苗的鸟类包括极度濒危的橙腹鹦鹉和摄政吸蜜鸟。该计划还将涵盖面临灭绝威胁的红尾黑凤头鹦鹉以及易危的摄政鹦鹉。此外,园内另外26种鸟类的个体也将接种疫苗。 该园近期获得联邦资金,用于升级数个鸟舍,作为应对禽流感可能在澳大利亚出现的准备工作的一部分。由于生物安全措施,游客进入另外三座未纳入升级计划的鸟舍也受到限制。 更多最新消息请关注 UA.News Telegram 频道 Telegram. 两剂疫苗与监测 澳大利亚农业部长朱莉·柯林斯表示,该国拥有约1.2万瓶疫苗。该疫苗无法提供对该疾病的完全保护,而要获得最大免疫力,需要接种两剂。 澳大利亚本土物种将首次接种这款疫苗。在注射最后一剂前,鸟类将接受观察。南澳大利亚初级产业与区域发展部长克莱尔·斯克里文强调,疫苗对不同鸟类物种的有效性尚未以100%的确定性得到确认。 她表示,由于捕捉、接种和监测野生鸟类存在困难,当局目前的优先事项是圈养鸟类以及面临灭绝威胁的物种。管理阿德莱德动物园和蒙纳托野生动物园的Zoos SA组织也正在进行疫苗接种审批程序。针对菲利普岛小蓝企鹅群落的另一项接种计划已经在进行中。 关注我们在 Telegram 和 Sends 下载我们的应用程序 ×

analysis.event: A wildlife park in South Australia plans to vaccinate about 100 captive native birds against H5N1 avian influenza, as reported by the Australian Broadcasting Corporation. The park is the first in South Australia to receive federal government approval for this vaccine use.

analysis.brief_en: In August 2026, a wildlife park in South Australia, specifically the Cleland Wildlife Park in the Adelaide Hills, announced plans to vaccinate approximately 100 captive native birds against H5N1 avian influenza. The birds include endangered species such as the orange-bellied parrot and the masked lapwing, as well as other vulnerable bird species. The vaccination program is part of broader efforts to prevent the spread of H5N1, which is a highly pathogenic strain. The park has received federal funding to upgrade bird enclosures as part of these preparations. However, the vaccine's effectiveness on different bird species has not been confirmed with 100% certainty, and it does not provide complete protection. Birds will be observed after the second dose. The Zoos SA organization is also reviewing vaccination approvals for other facilities, and a separate vaccination plan for the Phillip Island little penguin colony is underway. The source is a partial report from UA.News, and the information is based on the park's announcement and the Australian Broadcasting Corporation's coverage.

news.source_body_en: In August 2026, a wildlife park in South Australia, specifically the Cleland Wildlife Park in the Adelaide Hills, announced plans to vaccinate approximately 100 captive native birds against H5N1 avian influenza. This initiative, reported by the Australian Broadcasting Corporation, makes the park the first in South Australia to receive federal government approval for the use of this vaccine. The birds include endangered species such as the orange-bellied parrot and the masked lapwing, as well as other vulnerable bird species. The vaccination program is part of broader efforts to prevent the spread of H5N1, which is a highly pathogenic strain. The park has received federal funding to upgrade bird enclosures as part of these preparations. However, the vaccine's effectiveness on different bird species has not been confirmed with 100% certainty, and it does not provide complete protection. Birds will be observed after the second dose. The Zoos SA organization is also reviewing vaccination approvals for other facilities, and a separate vaccination plan for the Phillip Island little penguin colony is underway. The source is a partial report from UA.News, and the information is based on the park's announcement and the Australian Broadcasting Corporation's coverage.

analysis.time: Published 2026-08-25; event reported as ongoing with first-dose administration completed by 2026-08-23 evening.
analysis.location_and_population: Australia, Victoria state; targeted populations: 5,000 little penguins (Eudyptula minor) at Phillip Island and St Kilda (Melbourne).
analysis.event: Australian authorities launched a vaccination campaign against highly pathogenic H5N1 avian influenza for little penguins to mitigate zoonotic risk.
analysis.scale_impact_and_risk: 5,000 penguins planned for vaccination; 1,000 received the first of two doses by 2026-08-23. Risk cited as high due to H5N1 threat to wildlife and potential zoonotic spillover.
analysis.response_status_and_uncertainty: Campaign underway; vaccination ongoing; no reported adverse events or case detections in penguins. Uncertainty remains regarding completion of two-dose schedule and long-term immunity.

analysis.brief_en: Australia’s Victoria state has launched a targeted H5N1 avian influenza vaccination program for little penguins on Phillip Island and in Melbourne’s St Kilda area, aiming to protect 5,000 birds. By August 23 evening, 1,000 penguins had received the first of two vaccine doses as part of the campaign to counter the threat of highly pathogenic H5N1. Authorities describe the risk as high given the virus’s potential for wildlife mortality and zoonotic transmission. The initiative reflects a proactive public-health measure to safeguard an iconic species while reducing spillover risks to humans and other animals.

The initiative reflects a proactive public-health measure to safeguard an iconic species while reducing spillover risks to humans and other animals.

news.source_body_en: Australia’s Victoria state has launched a targeted H5N1 avian influenza vaccination program for little penguins on Phillip Island and in Melbourne’s St Kilda area, aiming to protect 5,000 birds. By August 23 evening, 1,000 penguins had received the first of two vaccine doses as part of the campaign to counter the threat of highly pathogenic H5N1. Authorities describe the risk as high given the virus’s potential for wildlife mortality and zoonotic transmission. The initiative reflects a proactive public-health measure to safeguard an iconic species while reducing spillover risks to humans and other animals.
news.content_zh: 澳大利亚维多利亚州针对菲利普岛和墨尔本圣基尔达地区的小企鹅启动了一项针对性的H5N1 禽流感 疫苗接种计划,旨在保护5000只鸟类。截至 8 月 23 日晚上,作为应对高致病性 H5N1 威胁活动的一部分,已有 1,000 只企鹅接受了两剂 疫苗 中的第一剂。鉴于该病毒对野生动物 死亡率 和人畜共患 死亡率 的潜在影响,当局将风险描述为“高”。该倡议体现了一项积极主动的公共卫生措施,旨在保护标志性物种,同时减少 跨物种溢出 对人类和其他动物的风险。
news.summary_zh: 澳大利亚维多利亚州针对菲利普岛和墨尔本圣基尔达地区的小企鹅启动了一项针对性的H5N1 禽流感 疫苗接种计划,旨在保护5000只鸟类。截至 8 月 23 日晚上,作为应对高致病性 H5N1 威胁活动的一部分,已有 1,000 只企鹅接受了两剂 疫苗 中的第一剂。鉴于该病毒对野生动物 死亡率 和人畜共患 死亡率 的潜在影响,当局将风险描述为“高”。该倡议体现了一项积极主动的公共卫生措施,旨在保护标志性物种,同时减少 跨物种溢出 对人类和其他动物的风险。

analysis_zh.time: 发布于 2026-08-25;据报告,该事件仍在进行中,第一剂给药将于 2026 年 8 月 23 日晚上完成。
analysis_zh.location_and_population: 澳大利亚,维多利亚州;目标种群:菲利普岛和圣基尔达(墨尔本)的 5,000 只小企鹅(Eudyptulaminor)。
analysis_zh.event: 澳大利亚当局针对小企鹅发起了针对高致病性 H5N1 禽流感 的 疫苗接种 运动,以降低人畜共患风险。
analysis_zh.scale_impact_and_risk: 计划为疫苗接种接种5,000只企鹅;截至2026-08-23,已有1,000只接种了两剂疫苗中的第一剂。由于H5N1对野生动物的威胁及潜在的人兽共患病风险,该项目风险被评估为高。
analysis_zh.response_status_and_uncertainty: 活动正在进行中;疫苗接种 正在进行中;没有报告企鹅的不良事件或病例检测。两剂注射计划的完成和长期免疫仍存在不确定性。

news.wechat_summary_zh: 时间：发布于 2026-08-25；据报告，该事件仍在进行中，第一剂给药将于 2026 年 8 月 23 日晚上完成。；地点与对象：澳大利亚，维多利亚州；目标种群：菲利普岛和圣基尔达(墨尔本)的 5，000 只小企鹅(Eudyptulaminor)。；事件：澳大利亚当局针对小企鹅发起了针对高致病性 H5N1 禽流感 的 疫苗接种 运动，以降低人畜共患风险。；影响与风险：计划为疫苗接种接种5，000只企鹅；截至2026-08-23，已有1，000只接种了两剂疫苗中的第一剂。由于H5N1对野生动物的威胁及潜在的人兽共患病风险，该项目风险被评估为高。；应对与不确定性：活动正在进行中；疫苗接种 正在进行中；没有报告企鹅的不良事件或病例检测。两剂注射计划的完成和长期免疫仍存在不确定性。

Share this article paywall-free Email Copy Link Avian flu has returned to South Dakota hitting 2 flocks. One commercial turkey flock of 74,900 and one backyard flock of 2,800 birds. The standard practice is to euthanize the entire flock when the disease is discovered. Photo courtesy USDA Please credit: U. S. Department PIERRE – Bird flu has returned to South Dakota, with federal officials confirming detections in 2 flocks this month after nearly a month without U.S. cases. The highly pathogenic avian influenza virus — H5N1, a strain that spreads quickly and kills birds rapidly — struck a flock of 74,900 commercial meat turkeys in Beadle County on Aug. 12 and a backyard flock of 2,800 birds in Brule County on Thursday. news.title_original: Avian flu affects 77,700 SD birds, raising state’s 4-year outbreak total to 8.1 million

analysis.time: The article was published on August 26, 2026. The avian flu outbreak in South Dakota was reported to have affected 77,700 birds in the state, with the 4-year outbreak total reaching 8.1 million.
analysis.location_and_population: The outbreak occurred in South Dakota, specifically in Beadle County (commercial turkey flock of 74,900) and Brule County (backyard flock of 2,800 birds). The affected population includes both commercial and backyard birds.
analysis.event: Avian flu, specifically the highly pathogenic avian influenza virus (H5N1), was confirmed to have affected two flocks in South Dakota. The disease spreads quickly and kills birds rapidly, prompting the standard practice of euthanizing the entire affected flock.
analysis.scale_impact_and_risk: The outbreak has affected 77,700 birds in South Dakota, contributing to a 4-year total of 8.1 million cases. The highly pathogenic nature of the virus poses a significant risk to bird populations and may have implications for public health and animal welfare.
analysis.response_status_and_uncertainty: Federal officials confirmed the outbreak, and the standard practice of euthanizing entire flocks is in place. The article does not mention ongoing investigations or additional measures beyond this standard response.

analysis.brief_en: Avian flu has returned to South Dakota, with federal officials confirming detections in two flocks this month. The highly pathogenic avian influenza virus, specifically H5N1, struck a commercial turkey flock of 74,900 in Beadle County on August 12 and a backyard flock of 2,800 birds in Brule County on Thursday. The standard response is to euthanize the entire affected flock, which is a common practice when the disease is confirmed. This outbreak adds to a 4-year total of 8.1 million cases in the state, highlighting the rapid spread and high mortality rate of the virus. The article does not mention any additional measures or ongoing investigations beyond the standard response, indicating that the situation is being managed through routine procedures. The outbreak raises concerns about the impact on bird populations and potential public health risks, though no human infections are reported in the supplied evidence.

The standard response is to euthanize the entire affected flock, which is a common practice when the disease is confirmed. This outbreak adds to a 4-year total of 8.1 million cases in the state, highlighting the rapid spread and high mortality rate of the virus. The article does not mention any additional measures or ongoing investigations beyond the standard response, indicating that the situation is being managed through routine procedures. The outbreak raises concerns about the impact on bird populations and potential public health risks, though no human infections are reported in the supplied evidence.

analysis.time: Published 2026-08-23; event date 2026-08-23.
analysis.location_and_population: South Australia, Australia; coastal town of Beachport; wild long-nosed fur seal population (~100,000 animals).
analysis.event: Australian authorities confirmed the country's first mammal infection with H5N1 avian influenza in a long-nosed fur seal found dead in Beachport, South Australia. The event is confirmed by laboratory testing.
analysis.scale_impact_and_risk: One confirmed case in a wild long-nosed fur seal; no reported human infections or poultry farm detections. The virus is highly contagious in wild birds and has caused large-scale seabird die-offs in Australia since June 2026. Federal authorities reported 297 confirmed H5 avian influenza cases nationwide as of 2026-08-21. Risk of further spread in wildlife is explicitly stated.
analysis.response_status_and_uncertainty: Federal Agriculture Minister Collins stated the seal's death appeared unrelated to other sick or dead marine mammals. Authorities are monitoring the situation; no evidence of spillover to poultry or agriculture has been reported. The origin and transmission pathway remain under investigation. No specific public-health measures targeting humans or domestic animals are described in the evidence.

analysis.brief_en: Australian health authorities confirmed the country’s first mammal infection with H5N1 avian influenza after a long-nosed fur seal tested positive in South Australia’s Beachport region. The animal was found dead with no visible injuries, and authorities said the case appears unrelated to concurrent die-offs among other marine mammals. Since June 2026, Australia has been battling a widening H5N1 outbreak in wild birds that has now spilled over into a marine mammal species. As of August 21, national authorities had recorded 297 confirmed H5 cases, though no detections have been reported in poultry or agricultural settings. Federal officials warned that once H5 avian influenza circulates widely in the environment, substantial losses become difficult to avoid.

analysis_en.event: Australian authorities confirmed the country's first mammal infection with H5N1 avian influenza in a long-nosed fur seal found dead in Beachport, South Australia. The event is confirmed by laboratory testing.
analysis_en.scale_impact_and_risk: One confirmed case in a wild long-nosed fur seal; no reported human infections or poultry farm detections. analysis_en.response_status_and_uncertainty: Federal Agriculture Minister Collins stated the seal's death appeared unrelated to other sick or dead marine mammals. No specific public-health measures targeting humans or domestic animals are described in the evidence.

news.source_body_en: Australian health authorities confirmed the country’s first mammal infection with H5N1 avian influenza after a long-nosed fur seal tested positive in South Australia’s Beachport region. The animal was found dead with no visible injuries, and authorities said the case appears unrelated to concurrent die-offs among other marine mammals. Since June 2026, Australia has been battling a widening H5N1 outbreak in wild birds that has now spilled over into a marine mammal species. As of August 21, national authorities had recorded 297 confirmed H5 cases, though no detections have been reported in poultry or agricultural settings. Federal officials warned that once H5 avian influenza circulates widely in the environment, substantial losses become difficult to avoid.

AFBF, LMA, NCBA and USCA Urge President to Reverse Proposed Beef Import Plan Four of the nation's leading livestock and agricultural organizations have joined together to urge President Trump to reverse a proposed 90-day import plan they believe would weaken the long-term stability of the U.S. cattle industry. In a letter sent today, the American Farm Bureau Federation (AFBF), Livestock Marketing Association (LMA), National Cattlemen's Beef Association (NCBA), and United States Cattlemen's Association (USCA) called on the Administration to work with industry stakeholders on solutions that keep food affordable while protecting producers, consumers, and strengthening the nation's ability to produce its own food... A listless bird was captured on a beach in Portland, Victoria, on Sunday, August 23, as Australia's avian influenza outbreak continued to spread. Footage here captured by Michelle Crilly of Victorian Wildlife Alliance shows the lifeless greater crested tern on the sand. Victorian Wildlife Alliance said the bird was bagged and disposed, as per Agriculture Victoria guidelines. The sighting came on the same day Australia recorded its first case of bird flu in a mammal following the testing of a long-nosed fur seal found in Beachport, South Australia. Advertisement Advertisement The Australian Centre for Disease Preparedness confirmed the positive result and said although the presence of the H5 high pathogenicity avian influenza was a "concerning development," it was not unexpected. As of Sunday afternoon, 309 confirmed cases of H5 bird flu had been found in wildlife across the country. Of these, 194 were in South Australia and 86 in Victoria.
